item.title: [dodgersway.com] Blake Snell bromance may be enough to convince Tarik Skubal to reach to stay with Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ranaudo
item.description: Whether you believe Tarik Skubal actually has a chance to sign with the Los Angeles Dodgers long-term or not, the relationship blossoming between him and Blake Snell right now is giving fans something to enjoy heading into the postseason. The two shared a moment in the clubhouse after Thursday's 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, a game that clinched Los Angeles' 13th NL West title in the last 14 seasons and its fifth in a row. Skubal called it "the first of many," Snell fired back that it's spec
item.content:encoded:
Whether you believe Tarik Skubal actually has a chance to sign with the Los Angeles Dodgers long-term or not, the relationship blossoming between him and Blake Snell right now is giving fans something to enjoy heading into the postseason.
The two shared a moment in the clubhouse after Thursday's 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, a game that clinched Los Angeles' 13th NL West title in the last 14 seasons and its fifth in a row.
Skubal called it "the first of many," Snell fired back that it's special "because you're playing this postseason with your boy," and Skubal's response, calling Snell his best friend and "little brother," is exactly the kind of dugout chemistry that makes a fanbase fall in love with a roster before any playoff game is played.
Star power gelling like this isn't as easy as it looks from the outside. I've been in enough clubhouses to know that talent alone doesn't guarantee chemistry, and sometimes the best player in the world never quite finds his footing in a new room.
That clearly hasn't been the issue here. Skubal and Snell have started pulling actual pranks on each other, knocking over one another's chairs in the clubhouse, and have leaned into Step Brothers-inspired jokes about becoming new best friends on social media.
Pitching coach Mark Prior summed it up simply: "He's just chill. You can joke around with him. You can talk to him." Those are the intangibles that matter just as much as mound presence, stuff and command once October arrives.
Baseball already has some precedent for this kind of bond becoming part of a team's identity. Kris Bryant and Anthony Rizzo built exactly that in Chicago on their way to breaking a 108-year championship drought in 2016, and a decade later, people are still throwing them reunion podcasts built around that friendship.
Why Scott Boras could still complicate a Tarik Skubal-Blake Snell reunion with Dodgers
Now for the reality check. Scott Boras has made a career out of pushing his best clients toward the open market, with Snell happening to be one of those clients, on his own five-year, $182 million deal signed in 2024 that runs through 2029, with a conditional option for 2030.
If Skubal follows his buddy, annd signs anywhere from three to five years this winter, that puts the two of them together in that rotation for at least three seasons and potentially four, right in the prime of their careers.
However, a meaningful friendship doesn't change Boras's feelings nor his instincts. It's still going to take a team's best offer (plus some likey gaudy contract incentives) to ultimately entice him to sign. What should give Dodgers fans a glimmer of hope is simpler than any friendship storyline, though.
Skubal has been outstanding since the trade, going 3-2 with a 2.52 ERA across eight starts in Dodger blue, looking every bit like a two-time Cy Young winner who's found his rhythm in a new clubhouse. He looks like he's having fun out there, and that has a way of translating into winning, which is ultimately the only thing this fanbase really cares about.
The bromance is funny and keeps things light when the whole world is watching your every move. The Boras conundrum is still the reality. But if the two ever turn this relationship into a marriage, a long-term deal that keeps Skubal in a Dodgers uniform next to his little brother, that's the version of this story Los Angeles fans are actually hoping for.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers esperan que Snell (ingle) haga una apertura más antes de la postemporada
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Dos días después de salir de su apertura tras apenas una entrada debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, Blake Snell lanzó desde 90 pies de distancia en el terreno del Dodger Stadium antes del primer juego de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes. Salió sintiéndose bien, y los Dodgers creen que evitaron lo peor con una lesión que ha sido un problema recurrente a lo largo de la carrera del zurdo.
"Feliz de que lo detectamos a tiempo", indicó el manager Dave Roberts, quien señaló que Snell no fue enviado a hacerse ninguna prueba de imagen.
Los Dodgers se mantienen optimistas de que el dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young hará otra apertura en la temporada regular en algún momento durante sus nueve juegos restantes. El día específico está por verse -- su turno regular en la rotación caería durante la serie de tres choques de Los Ángeles ante San Diego que comienza el martes -- pero no se espera que lance con ninguna limitación.
"Creo que sería más una apertura normal", aseguró Roberts. "Tal vez no lo exijamos muchísimo, dado que no sabemos cómo se desarrollará la temporada. Pero esta será su última salida de la temporada regular, así que creo que sería más una apertura regular".
This browser does not support the video element.
Snell inició la campaña en la lista de lesionados de 15 días con fatiga en el hombro izquierdo, haciendo su debut de temporada apenas el 9 de mayo. Casi de inmediato volvió a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en su codo izquierdo, los cuales fueron removidos mediante el procedimiento NanoNeedle Scope. Desde que regresó el 11 de agosto, Snell ha lucido como si no hubiera perdido el ritmo, registrando efectividad de 1.01 en siete aperturas, con 47 ponches y 14 bases por bolas en 35.2 entradas.
Para un lanzador que comparte la rotación con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tarik Skubal, Snell es una pieza absolutamente vital en los planes de los Dodgers para los playoffs. Si su condición empeora, la profundidad del pitcheo abridor de Los Ángeles de repente luce bastante mermada. Está Tyler Glasnow, quien abrió el viernes contra San Francisco pero que ha lidiado con sus propios problemas de lesiones este año. También se espera que Roki Sasaki (fuera desde el 27 de agosto por una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho) regrese pronto para una última apertura en la temporada regular.
Dada la historia de Snell de lanzar bien luego de largas ausencias de acción en Grandes Ligas, ¿han considerado los Dodgers permitirle saltarse su próxima apertura, que siga descansando y esperar a que vuelva a la loma una vez que comiencen los juegos de postemporada?
"Se ha pensado en eso", reveló Roberts. "Pero todavía estás hablando de unos posibles 17 días, algo así... es mucho tiempo para no estar en competencia. Donde normalmente, con su historial, todavía tienes rehabilitaciones y cosas por el estilo. Así que no es sólo cuestión de conectarlo y ya, que descanse dos semanas y lance en un juego de playoffs".

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Dalton Rushing's treatment, Dodgers optimistic with Pages, Snell & Ohtani

Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent
item.content:encoded:
With just over one week left in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still looking to secure the No. 2 seed in the National League postseason bracket and perhaps more importantly, get to a better state of health.
Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent start due to left groin tightness.
Dodgers updates
Blake Snell
Snell played catch from flat ground on Friday, getting out to 90 feet as signs point to avoiding the 15-day injured list.
“I’m very hopeful that he’ll make a start before the end of the season,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Snell has a history of missing roughly one month because of adductor/groin strains, but he and the team believe the latest issue did not advance to being that significant.
“Don’t know the answer exactly,” Roberts said when asked what may have caused the tightness, “but happy that we caught it early.”
If — or when — Snell does pitch again, Roberts indicated it would be a normal start rather than an abbreviated final tuneup before the postseason begins.
Andy Pages
After previously sharing the expectation is for Pages to return during the homestand, Roberts offered a slightly more concrete timeline by saying that should come during the Dodgers’ series against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing
According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, Rushing received a PRP injection in his right forearm.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out.
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 18, 2026
Rushing had a brief return at the start of September after going on the 10-day injured list last month because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow. The Dodgers have suggested a best-case scenario is to have Rushing available as a pinch-hit option off the bench in the playoffs.
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani took swings against a coach pitching in the batting cage and “came out of it well,” per Roberts. Although the superstar talent is making progress, Roberts said more clarity won’t come until Ohtani faces live pitching or hits off the Trajekt machine.
“But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts added.
Roki Sasaki
Roberts further confirmed Sasaki is nearing a return and will start despite the prior plan being to shift him into a bullpen role. Some of the change is due to the uncertainty that arose from Snell’s groin trouble.
However, Sasaki still figures to be utilized as a reliever in the postseason if the Dodgers rotation remains healthy.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers have no choice. They must hope Tyler Glasnow can trust himself in the playoffs
item.dc:creator: Mirjam Swanson
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The oft-injured Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title. - Glasnow fought through early struggles to throw six innings and strike out 10 in an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, but can he replicate that in the playoffs? - The veteran right-hander played a key role in the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series, and the team will need him to do
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The oft-injured Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
- Glasnow fought through early struggles to throw six innings and strike out 10 in an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, but can he replicate that in the playoffs?
- The veteran right-hander played a key role in the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series, and the team will need him to do the same this October.
The Dodgers are all in, going for a three-peat.
And they might not have an extra ace up their sleeve anymore, but when the postseason begins, they’ll still hope to play their quad of aces — four of a kind that will beat almost every other hand.
But do the Dodgers have four aces? Or three? Or just a pair, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal?
Could the left groin tightness that chased Blake Snell from his last start after an inning linger into the postseason? Snell isn’t the sturdiest of starters, having missed most of the season because of shoulder fatigue and loose bodies in his left elbow. But the Dodgers suggest he’s going to be OK; Snell is slated for one last regular-season start.
And what about Tyler Glasnow?
Tyler Glasnow gives up just three hits and strikes out 10, and Mookie Betts hits two home runs in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Can the Dodgers trust the 6-foot-8 right-hander who missed three months because of back spasms?
Should they put their belief in the 11th-year pitcher who likely would be the odd man out in the postseason if Shohei Ohtani still were available to deal on the mound?
They’re going to have to trust Glasnow. And he’s going to have to trust himself.
“He’s a guy that you can’t put too much thought into him, or it starts getting in his own head,” said catcher Dalton Rushing, who is injured but enjoyed watching Glasnow find his footing in Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
“It was a lot of fun to watch tonight,” Rushing said. “Looked like himself.”
After three suboptimal innings, Glasnow settled down in a trust-building exercise of an outing against the Giants and their triple A-caliber lineup.
He wasn’t the most efficient, the most pristine, the sharpest — but he was fit to throw 98 pitches and six innings.
To fight through after laboring with 59 pitches in the first three innings, to earn his second win since April and to help the Dodgers maintain their four-game buffer over the Atlanta Braves as they play to secure a first-round bye with eight games left.
There was no champagne hangover for Glasnow on Friday — he flew directly back to L.A. from Miami, skipping Thursday’s clubhouse party in Cincinnati, where the Dodgers celebrated clinching the National League West Division for the 13th time in 14 years — but how about a toast to good health?
Cheers to giving up just two runs, one each in the second and third innings. To walking only two batters and striking out 10. To giving up only three hard hits and producing 15 whiffs.
To feeling and pitching better.
“After that third inning, I just stopped trying to be quick,” Glasnow said. “Just go out and be athletic, and I think it started to feel a little bit more timed up.”
Glasnow came into Friday’s game — one of his final two regular-season starts — having given up eight runs on 11 hits and seven walks in his previous two starts, looking less than comfortable in both. Out of rhythm, out of sync.
“This is an important start, and he knows it,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s certainly not do or die, but ... just to kind of get back feeling good.”
Afterward, Roberts wasn’t thrilled with how Glasnow started, but liked how he finished.
“You could see him fighting himself a little bit,” Roberts said. “The fastball command wasn’t great early. Got a lot of strikeouts. Curveball wasn’t sharp. But I thought he did a good job of making pitches when he needed to. The slider got better, fastball command got better as the game went on. Good to see him get through six innings.”
It’ll be better yet for the Dodgers’ odds if Glasnow can carry Friday’s progress into his next start — and then into the playoffs, where he proved himself as a Dodger last season after an elbow sprain sidelined him for the 2024 postseason.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
In the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, Glasnow made six appearances, three of them starts. He had a 1.69 ERA and averaged 10.5 strikeouts per nine innings. The stuff of aces.
“Today was a step in the right direction,” said Glasnow, the formerHart High School star, before leaving the clubhouse in flip-flops. “I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff, and have a good one right before playoffs.
“I think I’m in a good spot right now.”

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter

Mookie Betts finished with two home runs. With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important box
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
- The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs.
With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important boxes on their postseason to-do list.
They clinched a playoff berth for a record-tying 14th straight season and won the division title for the fifth time in a row. And with Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers (94-60) also have an outside shot at their fourth 100-win season in six years.
But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a lot of work to do between now and the start of the playoffs — the most important task being determining exactly where and when they’ll open the postseason.
With Friday’s win and the Milwaukee Brewers’ victory in Baltimore, the Dodgers trail the Brewers by two games in the race for the league’s best record and the home-field advantage in the postseason that goes with it. They also lead the Atlanta Braves by four games for the league’s second-best record, which would give them a first-round playoff bye and an extra five days to get their sizable contingent of walking wounded healthy.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
“To get one of these top two seeds is important. And our guys understand that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Winning the division is great, but I still think our best baseball is ahead of us.”
Achieving that, however, will require emptying an injury list that is almost as long as the team’s starting lineup. If the season ended today, the Dodgers would have at least seven players who wouldn’t be ready to play.
The Dodgers are also hopeful left-hander Blake Snell, who came out of Wednesday’s game after an inning with groin tightness, will be healthy enough to return for one more regular-season start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who shares the team lead in RBIs with Shohei Ohtani despite missing a month with a fracture in his left hand, is expected to be activated for the series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday, while backup catcher Dalton Rushing is swinging a bat and will hit against a pitching machine this weekend.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in a bullpen session Wednesday and could come off the IL next week but right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, second among Dodger relievers in innings and strikeouts, will miss the rest of the regular season with a back strain. He could join the team for the playoffs.
Then there’s Ohtani, the four-time MVP. He’s dealing with injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He has resumed taking batting practice and is eligible to come off the IL Wednesday. Roberts said he hopes to get Ohtani 10-12 at-bats before the playoffs.
“I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP,” Roberts said. “He’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
One player who did return was closer Edwin Díaz. Limited by multiple injuries to just 16 appearances this season, he was activated off the injured list Friday and threw 17 pitches in the ninth, giving up a single and striking out two batters.
For Roberts, the last month has looked like an episode of “The Pitt,” with medical crises piling up, one atop the other. Yet that’s hardly slowed the Dodgers, who opened their final homestand of the season having won 11 of their past 14 games.
Now the focus becomes continuing that momentum while getting as close to full strength as possible.
“They can go hand in hand,” Roberts said. “We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games, at the same time making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts.”
The Dodgers got a big lift Friday from rookie Josue De Paula, a player who didn’t figure in their postseason plans until a week ago, when he was called up to take Ohtani’s place. In his Dodger Stadium debut, De Paula singled and scored on a Teoscar Hernández single in the fifth, then roped a double to the wall in right-center an inning later, scoring Kyle Tucker to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Tucker, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Will Smith all homered in a five-run eighth inning, turning a nail-biter into a comfortable win.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns are being sued for allegedly failing to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers.
That gave right-hander Tyler Glasnow (5-1) his second win since April 23. Glasnow gave up just three hits in six innings, striking out a season-high 10 batters.
Hernández, who had two hits, is batting .368 with 17 RBIs in September; Tucker, who also had two hits, is hitting .424 with five home runs and 13 runs scored in his past 10 games; while Betts, with two homers Friday, has six hits in his past eight at-bats, lifting his average to a season-high .254.
That’s helped make up for Freddie Freeman’s struggles. Freeman, who went hitless in four at-bats Friday, striking out twice, has just six hits — and 13 strikeouts — in his last 48 at-bats.
“We still have a lot of work to do,” Roberts said before the game.
They have just over a week left to get it done.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip. They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top s
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip.
They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed with just nine games to go before October.
But perhaps taking priority over chasing playoff positioning, Roberts expressed confidence that the Dodgers could finish the season relatively healthy with both Shohei Ohtani and Blake Snell progressing well in the final two weeks of the regular season.
"I think it's about winning games, all the while ... getting our players back to health. But I think they can go hand in hand," Roberts said. "We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch

item.title: [MLB.com] Snell (groin) expected to start again for Dodgers before postseason

He emerged feeling good, with the Dodgers believing they avoided the worst with an injury that’s been a recurring issue throughout the left-hander’s career. “Happy that we caught it early,” said manager Dave Roberts, who noted that Snell was not sent to receive any imaging. The Dodg
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Two days after he exited a start following just one inning due to left groin tightness, Blake Snell threw from 90 feet on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants. He emerged feeling good, with the Dodgers believing they avoided the worst with an injury that’s been a recurring issue throughout the left-hander’s career.
“Happy that we caught it early,” said manager Dave Roberts, who noted that Snell was not sent to receive any imaging.
The Dodgers remain optimistic that the two-time Cy Young Award winner will make another regular-season start sometime during their remaining nine games. The specific day is to be determined -- his regular spot in the rotation would come up during L.A.’s three-game series vs. San Diego that begins on Tuesday -- but he is not expected to pitch with any limitations.
“I think it'd be more of a normal start,” said Roberts. “Maybe not pushing him a ton, given that we don't know how the season's going to play out. But this will be his last regular-season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start.”
Snell began the season on the 15-day injured list with left shoulder fatigue, not making his season debut until May 9. He almost immediately went back on the IL due to loose bodies in his left elbow, which were removed using the NanoNeedle Scope procedure. Since returning on Aug. 11, Snell has looked like he hasn’t missed a beat, pitching to a 1.01 ERA over seven starts, with 47 strikeouts and 14 walks in 35 2/3 innings.
For a pitcher who shares a rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, Snell is an absolutely vital part of the Dodgers’ postseason rotation plans. Should his condition worsen, the Dodgers’ starting pitching depth suddenly looks pretty thin. There’s Tyler Glasnow, who started on Friday against San Francisco but has dealt with injury issues of his own this year. Roki Sasaki (out since Aug. 27 with a right middle finger blister) is also expected to return soon for one final regular-season start.
Given Snell’s history of pitching well following long layoffs from Major League action, have the Dodgers given any consideration to letting him skip his next start, continuing to rest and waiting to have him pitch again once postseason games get underway?
“There is a thought,” said Roberts. “But you're still talking about a potential 17 days, something like that -- that's a long time to not be in competition. Where typically, with his history, you still have rehabs and things like that. So it's just not kind of a plug-and-play, sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game.”

item.content:encoded:
MARLINS (AP) — Kyle Tucker conectó el sexto grand slam de su carrera y se quedó a un doble de completar el ciclo por los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, quienes vencieron el viernes 6-2 a los Marlins de Miami para ampliar a ocho triunfos su mejor racha de la temporada.
Tucker conectó un sweeper en cuenta de 1-1 del relevista Cade Gibson para poner la pizarra 6-1 en el séptimo inning. Pegó un sencillo en el primero y un triple en el sexto.
Max Muncy totalizó tres hits y una base por bolas, y Will Smith añadió un sencillo impulsor de carrera por los Dodgers, líderes de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Blake Snell (4-1) permitió una carrera y ponchó a ocho durante cinco innings y dos tercios, en los que toleró cuatro inatrapables.
Después de que los Dodgers tomaron una ventaja de 2-0 con el sencillo impulsor de Smith, el dominicano Agustín Ramírez conectó un doble impulsor que recortó la diferencia a 2-1. Victor Vodnik abrió el séptimo retirando rápidamente a Alex Freeland y al boricua Kiké Hernández, pero dio bases por bolas a Tommy Edman y Mookie Betts y permitió un sencillo de Muncy para llenar las bases, preparando el batazo de Tucker entre el jardín derecho y el central ante Gibson.
El dominicano Otto López conectó cuatro hits y el venezolano Javier Sanoja conectó un triple y un sencillo por los Marlins, que han perdido siete de ocho y cuatro seguidos. El abridor Ryan Gusto (1-5) permitió dos carreras con cinco hits.
El derecho otorgó tres bases por bolas y ponchó a tres.
Deportes AP: https://apnews.com/hub/deportes

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers hopeful to avoid worst-case scenario with injured star pitcher
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season. Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he wa
item.content:encoded:
So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season.
Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he was "very hopeful" in the left-hander's chances to get back on the mound before the beginning of the playoffs.
"Happy that we caught it early," Roberts said of Snell's injury.
Indeed, when Snell exited Wednesday's game after 19 pitches, it raised immediate concerns about the state of the Dodgers' rotation.
Given the injuries the team is dealing with in its bullpen and its offense's inconsistent form through the second half of the season, the Dodgers will almost certainly need to lean on their starters during the playoffs — similar to the way they did last year, when a rotation of Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Shohei Ohtani (who will effectively be replaced by Tarik Skubal this year) carried the pitching staff to a second consecutive World Series title.
Losing Snell — who was already sidelined for three months earlier this season following an elbow procedure and has a history of left groin injuries throughout his career — would have dealt a massive blow to those plans.
However, the Dodgers are at least initially optimistic they've avoided anything close to a worst-case scenario.
While Roberts acknowledged that there is still "a little bit of uncertainty" regarding Snell, and no exact date for when he might pitch again, the skipper also noted that the two-time Cy Young Award winner didn't require medical imaging; another sign of the team's confidence that his injury was not more severe.
It's possible that, even if Snell continues to feel better, the Dodgers could elect to rest him for the remainder of the regular season to ensure he doesn't suffer any further setbacks before the playoffs.
But, they are also wary of giving Snell too long of a layoff entering the postseason.
"It's not just kind of plug-and-play," Roberts said, "[to] sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game."
Thus, the team will continue to monitor Snell's progress in the coming days, hopeful that a potential pitching crisis has been averted.
"We feel confident," Roberts said.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are beginning their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have just nine more games in the regular season. After clinching the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years, they're still battling for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves.
If the Dodgers clinch one of the top two seeds, they'll secure a first-round bye. That is especially crucial this season as the team deals with injuries to a handful of key players.
Here's the latest updates on six of those players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Friday that Ohtani is continuing to progress in his swinging progression.
“Everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three, four, five days," Roberts said. "He’s in a good spot.”
Ohtani has not yet progressed to hitting in live batting practice or off the Trajekt machine. Thus, a return doesn't appear to be imminent.
Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are aiming to get over their National League West celebration hangover by beating rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers clinched the division on Thursday, and there were a ton of celebrations, alcoholic bottles popped after the game, including a long flight to Los Angeles for the start of their six-game homestand.
Dodgers’ Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Will Smith, C
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Kyle Tucker, RF
7. Kike Hernandez, 3B
8. Alex Call, CF
9. Josue De Paula, DH
The Dodgers are facing a southpaw and are promoting some of their best hitters up the order. Betts, Hernandez, Smith, and Rojas are all putting together their best work at the plate against lefties.
Additionally, Alex Call gets a turn at center field, replacing Tommy Edman.
Josue De Paula gets a chance to prove himself against a lefty, which could help set up Betts and Smith at the top of the order with a baserunner to cash in.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are rolling out Tyler Glasnow, who has looked shaky compared to his usual standard. While there will be understandable rust for someone out months on the injured list.
He has a 4.91 ERA though 22 innings since return from the injured list with back spasms. In his most recent outing, the tall righty allowed four runs off five hits and four walks, with seven strikeouts.
Glasnow only provided four inning as well.
Heading into such a key stretch with the postseason around the corner, Glasnow has the chance to ease any doubts over his ability to deliver a quality playoff start.
With Blake Snell injured and facing an uncertain timeline, there is more riding on Glasnow than ever.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers begin their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers (93-60) clinched the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years on Thursday. The Giants (64-89) are a whopping 29 games behind LA in the division.
“It’s a big deal. It’s not easy,” manager Dave Roberts said of his team winning another NL West title. “I think a lot of people think it’s easy, it’s a rite of passage. But it’s not easy to win a division when everyone is gunning for you, to keep everyone motivated to play over the course of 162. It’s something we’re all really proud of. But that’s not the end goal.”
The Dodgers and Giants play six times over the next 10 days to close out the season. The Dodgers are just 3-4 against the Giants this season.
Dodgers vs Giants Pitching Matchup on Friday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the ball for the Dodgers on Friday night amid a concerning stretch of play.
The right-hander has allowed four runs in each of his last two starts. After his most recent one, manager Dave Roberts somewhat ominously said Glasnow "didn’t feel great" going into it.
Glasnow has made four starts since coming off the IL after a four-month absence due to a back injury. He left the team to go home early this week instead of traveling with them to Cincinnati as the staff wanted to have him avoid going on two flights.
The Dodgers will hope for better results from him on Friday, especially after Blake Snell left his Wednesday start with a groin injury.
For what it's worth, Glasnow's best start of the season came against the Giants in April, when he allowed one hit over eight shutout innings with nine strikeouts.
Opposite Glasnow will be left-hander Cesar Perdomo, who owns a 3.68 ERA over 14.2 career innings at the MLB level.
He made his debut on Sept. 1 as a reliever before starting each of his last two games.
Dodgers Lineup vs Giants
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, CF
- Josue De Paula, DH
Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound. Tommy Edman is also out.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Giants on Friday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Francisco Giants on Friday, Sept. 18 is 7:15 p.m. PT/10:15 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on Apple TV+.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GA — Gavin Stone and Bobby Miller delivered encouraging performances during their rehabilitation assignments this week, but Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts tempered expectations that either right-hander is close to claiming a significant role in the major-league pitching staff.
Stone threw four scoreless innings for Triple-A Oklahoma City, allowing one hit and striking out five. Miller followed with three scoreless innings, one hit allowed and five strikeouts. Their performances naturally raised questions about whether the Dodgers could use either pitcher during the final month of the regular season.
Roberts said both pitchers are progressing, but described their immediate value to the organization in one word.
“Right now, to be quite honest, I think it’s depth,” Roberts said.
Dodgers Temper Expectations for Stone and Miller
The Dodgers entered the season hoping Stone and Miller could eventually strengthen their pitching options, but injuries have prevented both from building a normal workload.
Stone has spent the entire season on the injured list with right shoulder inflammation after missing all of 2025 while recovering from shoulder surgery. He began his rehab assignment with Oklahoma City on August 6 and made his fourth appearance Wednesday.
The right-hander threw 58 pitches, including 41 strikes, and retired the final 10 batters he faced. It was his strongest performance since beginning the assignment and represented another positive step in a comeback that has required considerable patience.
Miller has been on the 60-day injured list all season because of right shoulder soreness. He began his Oklahoma City rehab assignment on August 5 and threw 49 pitches, including 33 strikes, during his three-inning outing Wednesday.
“They’re both doing well. They’re both coming back,” Roberts said. “But I think right now, to be quite honest, I think it’s depth.”
Health and Workload Remain the Priority
Roberts explained that both pitchers have experienced abbreviated seasons without enough competitive innings to immediately be considered finished products.
“Both those guys have had a very abbreviated season, not a lot of competitive baseball,” Roberts said. “And where we’re at on the calendar, I think it’s just getting these guys back to healthy and taking down starts or outings and sustaining that, which they both haven’t done in quite some time.”
That does not eliminate the possibility that Stone or Miller could contribute if the Dodgers need another arm. It does show that the organization is prioritizing their long-term recovery over forcing either pitcher into an immediate role because of one strong outing.
The Dodgers currently have a crowded rotation that includes Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Roki Sasaki. Shohei Ohtani is also nearing a return to game action, while Eric Lauer is available to provide length from the bullpen.
That depth gives Los Angeles the flexibility to let Stone and Miller continue rebuilding without rushing them. Roberts had previously discussed Stone as a possible multi-inning bullpen option down the stretch, but his latest comments indicate Stone must first prove he can sustain his workload.
Strong Rehab Outings Still Matter
Roberts’ caution should not erase the progress both pitchers have made. Stone and Miller returned to game action earlier this month after extended absences, giving the Dodgers two additional options who were unavailable for most of the season.
Their long-awaited returns to competitive pitching were important steps by themselves. Their latest results offer more evidence that the rehabilitation process is moving in the right direction.
For now, however, the Dodgers are viewing both starters as insurance rather than building their stretch-run plans around them. Stone and Miller must continue taking down innings, recovering well between appearances and showing that their shoulders can handle a consistent schedule.
If they accomplish that, the Dodgers could revisit their roles. Until then, their strongest contribution may be providing organizational depth while positioning themselves to enter next season healthy.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.dc:creator: Toran Flores

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced multiple injury scares in the pitching rotation. Still, they remain focused on preparing for a third straight World Series win.
One question about the Dodgers’ pitching centers on right-hander Roki Sasaki. The 24-year-old has been sidelined since revealing a blister on his throwing hand. He is eyeing a return before the postseason, although his role in Los Angeles’ rotation remains unknown.
Learning of Blake Snell’s recent groin injury has forced the Dodgers to pivot to a new strategy.
“To be safe, the Dodgers are likely to keep building up Roki Sasaki as a starter,” wrote The Athletic’s Katie Woo. “Sasaki threw a four-inning simulated game Wednesday in Cincinnati. While the Dodgers would prefer to use Sasaki in relief in the postseason, keeping him stretched out on a starter’s workload is smart insurance as they await further developments with Snell.”
Roki Sasaki’s Success as a Postseason Relief Pitcher
While struggling in his first year with the Dodgers in 2025, the team moved Roki Sasaki to a relief role during the postseason. This change worked out well for Los Angeles on its path to a World Series win.
Through nine appearances during the 2025 postseason, Sasaki finished with a 0.84 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, three saves, and two holds. He allowed just one earned run across his postseason run.
Sasaki transitioned into 2026 with similar struggled as the year prior. In 23 starts this season, the second-year starter has a 5-5 record, 4.60 ERA, and 1.33 WHIP across 119.1 innings pitched.
Los Angeles is preparing to have a stacked postseason rotation. It includes 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow.
Dodgers Are Closing in on a First-Round Bye
With a little over a week left of the MLB regular season, the Dodgers have their eyes set on clinching a first-round bye in the postseason. Earlier this week, Los Angeles earned the NL West title.
Now, finishing as a top-two team in the National League will secure a top seed and a much-needed break before their postseason run. Entering Friday, the Dodgers hold a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed.
The top position in the NL is also very much on the table. The Milwaukee Brewers currently own the spot, but hold just a two-game lead over the Dodgers.
It will definitely be something to monitor heading into the weekend. Los Angeles faces the San Francisco Giants in two separate series and the San Diego Padres to finish out their regular season.

item.content:encoded:
Why Dodgers' top rookie of 2026 is not Josue De Paula originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers have no shortage of talent.
Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, the NL West club has one of, if not the best, rosters in the Majors.
Concerns about the bullpen are warranted. But a starting three in the rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, and one of Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Justin Wrobleski is dominant.
With Ohtani on the IL, the Dodgers promoted a new talented prospect to replace him at designated hitter: slugger Josue De Paula.
De Paula promptly hit a homer just a few games into his first taste of the Majors and has a .789 OPS through 25 plate appearances.
But Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes it's too soon to label him the best Dodgers rookie of the season. Instead, Miller awarded that distinction to a middle infielder.
"There's already a case to be made for Josue De Paula in this spot, even though he just made his MLB debut as Shohei Ohtani's fill-in last Friday," Miller wrote.
"However, [Alex] Freeland spent much of the season as the Dodgers' primary second baseman, providing decent value with his glove while hitting just well enough to earn regular playing time."
Freeland doesn't have eye-popping offensive numbers, hitting .230 with four home runs and a 79 OPS+.
But he has +3 outs above average while playing at three infield spots, mainly second base.
De Paula could change Miller's mind during the final week of the regular season. Manager Dave Roberts should give him plenty of playing time.
For now, Freeland has done enough to warrant the title as the Dodgers' best rookie of the year.

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the California Post's weekly Dodgers recap, where we review the week that was, hand out very official awards and take stock of the state of the season.
PLAYER OF THE WEEK
Kyle Tucker (12-for-29 since Sept. 9; triple shy of the cycle on Thursday)
Off the bat, it appeared history was afoot.
Already on Thursday afternoon, Kyle Tucker had kicked his slow late-season turnaround into a suddenly more hopeful gear, hitting a two-run home run in the first, an RBI double in the second and a single that aided a three-run rally in the fourth.
Now, standing at the plate just a triple shy of the cycle in the eighth, he laced a line drive that made the feat feel possible.
With yet another squared-up swing, the $240 million slugger shot a ball into the left-center field gap. As two Reds outfielders converged on it, the entire Dodgers dugout rose in anticipation.
Alas, the 11th cycle in Dodgers history would have to wait.
The Reds turned a clean relay play. Tucker wisely — although, somewhat disappointingly, given the lopsided score — pulled up at second. And on the bench, all his teammates could do was razz him by mimicking send signs with their arms helplessly waving.
"I tried my best, but I don't think I was gonna get there," he told SportsNet LA afterward. "I probably would've been thrown out halfway."
Oh, well.
For this year's Dodgers, Tucker's 4-for-5, three-RBI game was still hugely encouraging, continuing what is now a weeklong surge in which the four-time All-Star has finally looked like himself.
Even before this stretch, the Dodgers committed to keeping Tucker as a key part of their lineup.
They hoped a breakthrough he made with his mechanics could salvage something from an otherwise disastrous debut campaign with the team.
Well, in his last eight games, Tucker has batted .414 with seven extra-base knocks, 10 RBIs and more walks (five) than strikeouts (four).
He has hit five home runs in his last 13 games, after collecting just 11 in his first 132 games this year.
It is the version of Tucker that the Dodgers will need in the playoffs, especially with fellow left-handed bats like Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman battling ongoing injuries.
After a season that once seemed so lost, signs of revival have arrived just in time.
PITCHERS OF THE WEEK
Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto (seven scoreless innings from each)
We are going with a tandem honor this week, from a pair of pitchers who will likely have the biggest influence on the Dodgers' World Series chances.
With Blake Snell battling a groin injury, and Tyler Glasnow entering a Friday start having recently regressed in his return from the injured list, the Dodgers' rotation doesn't feel quite as formidable as it once did.
Then again, if Skubal and Yamamoto keep pitching like they did this week — when they spun consecutive scoreless seven-inning outings in Cincinnati — those other question marks might not feel so daunting.
Both pitchers have sterling postseason track records: Yamamoto with a 7-1 record and 2.25 ERA in 10 playoff outings (including last year's World Series heroics) and Skubal with a 2-1 record and 2.04 ERA in six October appearances of his own (all with the Tigers the last two years).
Either could anchor a pitching staff on their own capable of making a run to the Fall Classic.
Together, they give the Dodgers arguably the best 1-2 punch in the majors. This week, they delivered the club's first pair of back-to-back scoreless seven-inning outings since 2022 when Tyler Anderson and Clayton Kershaw did it.
Granted, dominating the Reds in mid-September is not the same as producing gems in the playoffs.
But with so many other concerns mounting at the moment, Skubal and Yamamoto at least represent a pillar of potential pitching excellence to lean on, one that could compensate for other shortcomings in the Dodgers' three-peat bid.
PROSPECT OF THE WEEK
The entire Dodgers' minor-league system
The Dodgers' big-league club hasn't been the only one popping bottles in beer-soaked clubhouse celebrations recently.
This year, all four of the organization's minor-league affiliates also clinched places in their respective playoffs, with Triple-A Oklahoma City completing the quad-fecta by winning the second-half title in the Pacific Coast League on Wednesday.
It marks the first time the Dodgers have had four affiliates make the playoffs since 2019 (and that year included their now-defunct rookie-ball outpost in Ogden, Utah).
It's also the latest reminder about the strength of depth they boast in their highly touted farm system.
"I know people don't care about minor-league win percentages, but we kind of do," Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes told the California Post earlier this season. "I think it's a good proxy of how well your farm system is performing and how to understand what it takes to win."
Three of the club's affiliates have already been eliminated, with Double-A Tulsa, High-A Great Lakes and Single-A Ontario all losing in their division championship series.
OKC, meanwhile, will begin its postseason push next week in the best-of-three PCL Championship Series against the Athletics' Las Vegas affiliate. If they win that, they will remain in Vegas for the Triple-A National Championship Game against the winner of the International League.
QUESTION OF THE WEEK
Who should Dodgers hope to see in the first round of the playoffs?
With the NL West crown secured, the Dodgers still have work to do over the season's final nine games.
Given their injury problems, they've never needed a first-round bye so badly.
The good news: They remain four games up on the Braves for the NL's No. 2 seed, with their magic number down to six for securing passage straight to the NL Division Series.
And though they remain two games back of the Brewers for the best record in the majors — and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs — conventional wisdom in recent weeks has suggested that the playoff through the postseason might be better from the 2-seed anyway.
Now, however, the NL playoff field is getting muddied, with the red-hot Padres sitting just one game back of the Cubs and Phillies.
So, who should Dodgers fans root to see in a potential first-round matchup? Well, it depends on what kind of matchup you think suits the Dodgers best.
The Cubs and Phillies had seemed like tougher draws than the Braves or Padres, thanks to Chicago's deep and homer-happy lineup and the Phillies' powerhouse starting rotation trio.
But this week, Philadelphia lost one of its star pitchers, Jesús Luzardo, to a shoulder injury that has put his playoff availability in doubt. The Cubs, meanwhile, have seen their offense cool off and still face questions with an unimposing starting rotation.
The Braves have their own flaws (they've been a middle-of-the-pack offense since the All-Star break) but still boast Chris Sale at the top of their rotation.
The Padres, on the other hand, are making a familiar late-season surge and have a habit of playing the Dodgers tough in the playoffs.
It will all make for a fascinating final few days of scoreboard watching, with a slew of new postseason permutations now on the table.
The Dodgers, of course, won't be overly worried about who they might square off against. Their focus is on continuing to play a better brand of all-around baseball — and making sure they avoid the best-of-three wild-card round.

item.content:encoded:
In case you forgot or don’t know… the Los Angeles Dodgers won the NL West on Thursday afternoon, defeating the Reds 8-2.
LA celebrated in the Reds’ visiting clubhouse, giving the LA media access to all the players as they celebrated.
Reporters got a hold of ace starter Tarik Skubal, who shared an eyebrow-raising comment about the Los Angeles Dodgers’ future.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Announce 6 Roster Moves Before Astros Series
Tarik Skubal Gets Too Honest After Dodgers Clinching Moment
Per @SportsNetLA, here is a funny exchange between Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell:
Skubal: “It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many.”
Snell: “Tell em it’s gonna be special because you’re playing this postseason with your boy.”
Skubal: “This is my best friend; he’s my little brother.”
What I want to focus on, and something that’s been noted in other reports, is Skubal using the phrase “it’s gonna be the first of many”.
Skubal, of course, is an impending free agent after the season, so is he saying this will be the first of many division crowns with LA?? Or just generally in his career?? Hmmmm….
More MLB on Heavy: Josue De Paula Makes Honest Dodgers Statement After NL West Clinch
Tarik Skubal Since Joining the Dodgers
There haven’t been any public talks about Tarik Skubal’s upcoming contract demands, but baseball pundits believe it could be in the range of $350-400 million when all said and done.
After being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers, Tarik Skubal has been spectacular, per usual.
He’s made eight starts since joining LA, and Skubal has an ERA of 2.52 in 50 innings during that span with 57 strikeouts and a WHIP of 1.040.
Adding Skubal makes the Dodgers a dominant threat in the MLB playoffs, and LA will surely be a tough out come October.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Manager Doesn't Know if Blake Snell Will Pitch Again in Regular Season Amid Injury
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell left his Wednesday start after just one inning due to a groin injury he felt pregame. With just nine games to go in the regular season, including a crucial series against the San Diego Padres in which Snell is scheduled to start, the Dodgers are going to need the best out of their rotation moving forward. When it comes to Snell making that potential start, the left-hander expressed confidence he'd be able to. Manager Dave Roberts, however, was
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell left his Wednesday start after just one inning due to a groin injury he felt pregame.
With just nine games to go in the regular season, including a crucial series against the San Diego Padres in which Snell is scheduled to start, the Dodgers are going to need the best out of their rotation moving forward.
When it comes to Snell making that potential start, the left-hander expressed confidence he'd be able to. Manager Dave Roberts, however, was noncommittal.
“It’s a possibility,” Roberts said. “I like where his head is at, but he just can’t afford any more setbacks. So, whether it’s his next start or being pushed back or whatever it is, we’ve got to make sure that he comes out ready to go in the postseason.”
Despite feeling the groin injury before trotting to the mound to start the game, Snell still wanted to push through. However, after the first inning, he decided it was better to shut things down.
“I wasn’t trying to use my lower half. It was only a couple pitches where I got into my legs and threw the ball hard,” Snell said. “Outside of that, I was kind of guiding it in there.”
Snell has had a complicated history with his groin, including ending his 2021 season about a month early, missing a few weeks in 2022 and being sidelined for two months total over the course of the 2024 campaign.
Roberts was thankful that the southpaw didn't push further through his injury.
“Obviously happy that he alerted us early to get him out of the game, not make it worse,” Roberts said. “He told me that he felt some tightness in his left groin, and it didn’t loosen up. So obviously, the right decision was to get him out. I think, No. 1 is we’ll see how he comes in tomorrow, how he feels, get some more treatment and then when we get back to L.A., then we can make that decision if we want to get imaging."
Snell himself wants to make his next start, but only time will tell if he follows through or is watching from the dugout.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [NBC Sports] Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire: Josue De Paula holding his own, Victor Mesa Jr. back and mashing
