item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Waiver Wire Watch, our weekly fantasy baseball waiver wire guide. We’ll be doing things a little differently this season, with James Schiano publishing the initial waiver-wire article on Friday afternoon. Then Eric Samulski updates it every Sunday to make sure you get the most up-to-date information.
We’re doing things a little bit differently this time of year though. Rather than give a long list of players with deep analysis, there will only be a few dense player profiles for those we think currently need a bit more light shed on them. Otherwise, there will be long lists of players who can help your teams in a specific category or for this particular week.
The premise of the article is pretty straightforward. We’ll give you some recommended adds each week based on recent production or role changes. When we list a player, we’ll list the category where we think he’ll be helpful or the quick reason he’s listed. We hope this helps you determine whether the player fits your team’s needs. Not every “trending” player will be a good addition to your specific roster.
To qualify for this list, a player needs to be UNDER 40% rostered in Yahoo! formats. We understand you may say, “These players aren’t available in my league,” and we can’t help you there. These players are available in over 60% of leagues and some in 98% of leagues, so they’re available in many places, and that can hopefully satisfy readers who play in all league types.
⚾️Baseball is back on NBC: MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, “Opening Day” and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire Hitters
Jakob Marsee - OF, MIA (49% rostered)
(BATTING AVERAGE, OBP, COUNTING STATS PLAY)
Don’t let a dreadful start to the season distract you from how productive Marsee has been lately. Across nearly 200 plate appearances since the All-Star break, he’s slashing .287/.394/.482 with six home runs, 31 runs scored, and four stolen bases. Those four steals are a tad disappointing considering how often he ran last year and how often he’s gotten on base, but he’s a great source of hits and walks right now.
Victor Mesa Jr. - OF, TBR (26% rostered)
(POWER, SPEED, PLAYING TIME)
Mesa Jr. was activated off the injured list on September 1st after missing about two weeks with a hamstring strain and has gone right back to mashing. In 12 games since, he’s hitting .383 with three homers, 12 runs scored, eight RBI, and three stolen bases. He’s also sat three times, once against a right-handed pitcher (after playing consecutive days just off the IL) and twice against lefties. He’s also started against three lefties since, so he’s in a less stringent platoon than he was back in July and August. He’s been productive across the board whenever he’s played and could be reasonably relied upon in shallower leagues this week now with closer to a full-time role.
Josue De Paula - OF, LAD (12% rostered)
(HUGE PROSPECT PROMOTION, REAL POWER)
De Paula has held his own in one week of big league action with an .789 OPS across a measly 25 plate appearance sample entering play on Friday. That’s come in six starts – one of which against a left-handed pitcher – and he hit lead-off on Tuesday against a righty. He also sat in another game against a left-handed pitcher. In that small sample, we can see that he has plus bat speed to match his elite power pedigree. Also, he’s rarely chasing pitches out of the strike zone and making contact with the ones in it. He’s attempted two stolen bases too, but been caught once. This is all very encouraging after the 21-year-old left-handed slugger jumped straight from Double-A to the big leagues and may have the best offensive profile of any prospect in the minors. In 124 games this year with Tulsa, he hit 27 home runs and stole 31 bases with a .303/.401/.547 slash line. He also rarely struck out, took his walks, and can pull the ball in the air better than most other young players. Again, De Paula is as complete a hitter that we’ve seen called up to the majors recently.
Christian Encarnacion-Strand - 1B/3B, BAL (10% rostered)
(POWER, POST HYPE BREAKOUT?)
Encarnacion-Strand has enjoyed a late season renaissance since joining the Orioles. In 51 games, he has 10 home runs, 12 doubles, and an .846 OPS. That’s come with excellent power metrics like a 15.3% barrel rate and 73.6 mph bat speed. His hit tool and overall swing decisions remain concerning, but he’s a very legitimate power threat right now while he’s consistently putting his bat on the ball.
Leo Bernal - C, STL (3% rostered)
(PROSPECT PROMOTION, HOT STREAK)
The Cardinals promoted Bernal on September 1st when the rosters expanded and he’s started all 15 games since going 18-for-61 with three home runs, three doubles, and 15 RBI. He’s started 13 games at catcher, four at designated hitter, and one at first base over that span, so it’s clear the Cardinals are doing everything they can to get his bat in the lineup everyday. A switch-hitter with real power from each side of the plate, Bernal had 16 home runs, nine stolen bases, and a 115 wRC+ through 101 games at Triple-A this season as a 22-year-old with a strong underlying profile to match. He’s a great play in deep mixed or two-catcher leagues at the moment.
Emmanual Rodríguez - OF, MIN (2% rostered)
(PROSPECT CALL-UP, POSSIBLE POWER UPSIDE)
Rodríguez put together a solid first week in the big leagues going 5-for-23 with a home run, double, and triple. That’s come with a very high average bat speed at 77.1 mph – the same as Kyle Schwarber – but has struck out in one third of his plate appearances so far. He’s started all six games too and jumped up as high as fifth in the Twins’ order on Thursday. Rodríguez slashed .262/.414/.500 with 11 homers, 33 RBI, 36 runs scored, and seven steals across 220 Triple-A plate appearances this year, and, much like Walker Jenkins, could have been called up sooner had it not been for injuries. He rarely chases pitches out of the zone and makes plenty of hard contact, which is a combination we like. Considering he’s likely going to play a bunch and has real power, he could offer a spark this week.
Now, for big lists of players who can help you in specific categories plus, some who have good streaming schedules for the upcoming week.
Stolen Bases
Anthony Volpe - SS/2B, NYY
A.J. Ewing - OF, NYM
Max Clark - OF, DET
Brett Bateman - OF, TOR
Royce Lewis - 1B/2B/3B, MIN
Tommy Edman - 2B/3B/OF, LAD
Home runs
Bryce Eldridge - 1B, SFG
Jake Burger - 1B, TEX
Mickey Gasper - 1B/C, BOS
Carter Jensen - C, KCR
Griffin Conine - 1B/OF, MIA
Coby Mayo - 1B/3B, BAL
Counting Stats (Runs and RBI)
Alec Bohm - 1B/3B, PHI
Konnor Griffin - SS/OF, PIT
Travis Bazzana - 2B, CLE
Javier Sanoja - 2B/3B/SS/OF, MIA
Dustin Harris - OF, SDP
Dylan Beavers - OF, BAL
Nolan Arenado - 3B, ARI
Tim Tawa - 1B/2B/3B/OF, ARI
Connor Norby - 1B/2B/3B, COL
Walker Jenkins - OF, MIN
Streamers
Henry Bolte - OF, ATH
Zack Gelof - 2B/3B/OF, ATH
Lawrence Butler - OF, ATH
Cole Carrigg - SS/OF, COL
TJ Rumfield - 1B, COL
Kyle Karros - 3B, COL
Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire Pitchers
Emmet Sheehan - SP, LAD (53% rostered)
Blake Snell was removed from his start on Wednesday after one inning with left groin tightness. So, the recently optioned Sheehan might get another chance in the Dodgers’ rotation next week. Shuttled up and down a couple times recently, Sheehan returned to the big leagues for two starts after spending most of August in Triple-A and struck out 15 batters over two starts spanning 11 2/3 innings with just one earned run. He showed a renewed confidence in his fastball and that pitch was missing bats. Again, this is more speculative as Snell’s removal from his start appeared to be at least partially precautionary, but Sheehan could start at home against the Padres next week.
Justin Wrobleski - SP/RP LAD (41% rostered)
A pitcher’s upcoming schedule can be more important than their skill this time of year and Wrobleski is scheduled to face the Rafael Devers-less Giants twice to close the season. Bailey Ober and Zebby Matthews are also streaming options against the Giants. Overall, these are not a trio of pitchers we’d be running to recommend besides for this particular matchup.
Ryan Johnson - SP/RP, LAA (22% rostered)
As the Angels have overhauled their organizational pitching structure, many of their arms have made key adjustments over the last month. Johnson is part of that group, mostly trashing his sinker starting on August 11th. Since then, he has a 2.04 ERA across 39 2/3 innings. It’s still not a great profile – he’s a sidearming righty who doesn’t miss many bats and rarely throws a pitch over 90 mph besides that sinker – but he has a strong cutter, sweeper, and splitter. He’s scheduled to close the season with outings against the Twins and Mariners as a risky streaming option with good results lately.
Andrew Alvarez - SP/RP, WSN (22% rostered)
Alvarez is coming off a gem against the Angels last Saturday with a career-high seven scoreless innings, eight strikeouts, and just one hit allowed. He also walked four batters. In that game, the Angels ran out a lineup with nine right-handed hitters against the left-handed Alvarez and he tore through them with his curveball. His best pitch, it forced 10 of his 15 total whiffs and set up his auxiliary fastball and slider to get called strikes because hitters were so keyed in on the hook. His fastball leaves plenty to be desired at 92 mph with a suboptimal shape, but his curve and slider have a uniquely symbiotic relationship. David Laurila wrote about this on FanGraphs a few months back in an interview with Alvarez. Those two pitches have practically the same velocity and spin axis while the curveball has significantly more depth making hitters struggle to decipher between the two. He’s mildly trustworthy on Saturday against the Cardinals and again against the Mets next weekend.
Jonah Tong - SP, NYM (14% rostered)
Tong turned in another solid start on Monday against the Orioles going six strong with six strikeouts, one walk, and one unearned run. He pushed up his fastball usage heavily in this outing compared to his last, jumping up from 31% to 55% as he found a little bit of extra life on it. That could’ve been weather related as there was a brisk headwind in Citi Field that night – which can help pitchers add a bit of induced vertical break on their fastballs – but it was still the out-pitch Tong had envisioned. Off that dominant fastball, he was able to sequence his changeup, cutter, and curveball more effectively than he has otherwise against major league hitters and looked good overall. He has a huge test against the Phillies this Sunday to try and keep the momentum going before facing the Nationals next week to close the season.
Anthony Molina - RP/SP, SFG (5% rostered)
After being ripped for seven runs by the Padres last week, Molina bounced back well with 5 2/3 scoreless innings and six strikeouts on Tuesday against the Cardinals. He had much better command of his fastball in that more recent outing and that’s important for Molina because while that pitch has plus velocity around 96 mph, its shape is mediocre. So, it needs to be commanded in order to be consistently effective. Otherwise, that pitch is flanked by a quality curveball that’s effective against hitters from both sides of the plate, a solid slider, and a changeup that can miss bats against lefties. He’s scheduled to face the Twins at home next week to close his season.
Now, here are some long lists of other pitchers that could help you out this week. Be aware that schedules can often change this time of year and two-start pitchers can sometimes be a dice roll.

item.title: [MLB.com] Sasaki to make one more start for Dodgers before regular season concludes
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. The 24-year-old could be poised for a return to the 'pen for L.A.'s three-peat bid -- but he'll make at least one more start before the end of the regular season.
Sasaki has been sidelined since exiting his Aug. 26 start in Atlanta due to a blister on his right middle finger, and he should be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers' final homestand, likely in next week's series against the Padres.
The Dodgers had been considering getting Sasaki reacclimated to the bullpen before the postseason, but they kept the option of him starting open. Sasaki has remained stretched out during his time on the IL, most recently throwing four simulated innings on 48 pitches on Wednesday afternoon in Cincinnati.
"There's benefits both ways," manager Dave Roberts said. "One can argue it's best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up. Because if something does happen, he's built up. The other side is you can assimilate him into the 'pen and get comfortable in that role -- if that is the role. And so again, that's why we have to be really thoughtful with that."
On Wednesday night, the benefit of having additional rotation depth in Sasaki became clear when Blake Snell exited his start against the Reds after just one inning due to left groin tightness. Removing him from the game was seen as more of a precautionary move, but it exposed the somewhat tenuous state of the Dodgers' starting pitching at present.
If the projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow remain healthy, then the Dodgers will be in a great place. But there are question marks behind the Big Four. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch again this season. Justin Wrobleski moved to the bullpen and has been much shakier in the second half. Emmet Sheehan, who's currently with Triple-A Oklahoma City, is trending upward after his two most recent starts in the Majors -- but has been inconsistent overall.
Yamamoto is the only member of L.A.'s rotation who has not missed a start this season. Both Skubal and Snell had surgery to remove loose bodies from their left elbows. Glasnow spent more than three months on the IL due to lower back spasms, a recurring issue for him. The Dodgers have been proactive with managing Glasnow's back, as Roberts said he flew back to L.A. early to cut out an additional flight segment in between last Saturday's start in Miami and his next scheduled start on Friday.
Should anything happen to those four, Sasaki would figure to be the next arm up in the rotation. Sasaki has broken out in his second Major League season, even though his 5-5 record and 4.60 ERA may seem underwhelming at first glance. After a shaky start to the campaign, Sasaki introduced a new splitter and began to consistently throw his fastball harder, helping him achieve sustainable success as a starter. He posted a 2.63 ERA in seven starts before the blister issue arose.
Because Sasaki is returning from an injury, there may be some rust for him to knock off. He is still pitching with the blister, but Roberts said he felt good after covering it with Dermabond in his most recent bullpen session and simulated game.
"It's playable," Roberts said. "Given the Dermabond, the time that he'll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it's dang near close to being healed."
The Dodgers expect Sasaki to play an important role on their postseason pitching staff, even though they're not sure which role he'll fulfill -- but it is easier to shorten him up to pitch in relief rather than have to build him back up to start. After the latest injury concern, opting to keep starting on the table for Sasaki has already proven wise.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Reverse Roki Sasaki Return Plan After Blake Snell Injury
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki is set to return as a starter, though his postseason role remains unclear. The Dodgers’ plan changed after Blake Snell suffered an injury on Wednesday, September 16th, during his start against the Cincinnati Reds. Why the Dodgers changed plans Snell had a sore left groin and left after one inning. The southpaw was optimistic he avoided the worst of the injury, but the Dodgers still face uncertainty about his status. As a result, if Snell cannot pitch to fi
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki is set to return as a starter, though his postseason role remains unclear.
The Dodgers’ plan changed after Blake Snell suffered an injury on Wednesday, September 16th, during his start against the Cincinnati Reds.
Why the Dodgers changed plans
Snell had a sore left groin and left after one inning. The southpaw was optimistic he avoided the worst of the injury, but the Dodgers still face uncertainty about his status.
As a result, if Snell cannot pitch to finish the season or even the start of the postseason, the Dodgers will need to build up Sasaki as a starter to cover themselves.
Sasaki isn’t at his best right now — the Japanese righty is on the injured list with a blister on his middle finger.
He is eligible to be activated, and he just threw a 48-pitch live batting practice that went well, but the organization is waiting to see how they want to roll him out, either throw him in the bullpen now or have him make starts.
“One can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts said. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Will Roki Sasaki make a start?
After Snell’s injury, Roberts was asked again about Sasaki’s likelihood of returning as a starter rather than a reliever, and the skipper said that, to rest everyone properly and for build-up reasons, Sasaki will get a start at some point in the closing days of the season.
“You know, just trying to make sure that guys have ample rest,” Roberts said. “I think his next outing will be as a starter.”
While many fans thought it was a foregone conclusion that Sasaki would move into a reliever role, he could make his first-ever postseason start after a breakout campaign this year.
In his last seven games, he has a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts, 15 walks, and a 1.28 WHIP.
His splitter is a nasty putaway pitch that he throws for strikes, while the slider is coming along as a nice complement.
More importantly than his two offspeed pitches, his fastball sits in the high 90s and has more movement. With that profile, Sasaki would be a devastating postseason reliever, but now he may be called upon for a role no one expects.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West on Thursday afternoon.
With their 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, the Dodgers captured their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons. LA won the series over the Reds and is now 93-60.
Up next for LA? October baseball.
Following the victory over the Reds on Thursday, rookie prospect Josue De Paula made an honest statement about the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Mookie Betts Drops Heartfelt Message After Dodgers-Reds Game
Jose De Paula's Message to Dodgers After NL West Clinch
In Thursday's game, Josue De Paula went 1-for-4 with 1 RBI and a walk.
Here was his message following winning the NL West:
"Being on a winning team, I live for those special moments. I can't wait until we start winning in the playoffs. It's going to be cool."
De Paula hasn't played much with LA this season, as he's been busy tearing up the minors, but it's good he can't start wait until the team starts winning in October.
It also has to be a pretty cool moment for De Paula, who has been up with the Dodgers for all of a week and a half, and is already experiencing a division celebration champagne shower.
More MLB on Heavy: Tarik Skubal Sends Hilarious Message to Blake Snell After Reds Win
Josue De Paula's Early Showings in MLB
So far, De Paula has played in just six games for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Across 14 at-bats, he has two hits, including a home run, two runs scored, six walks, and an OPS of .829.
It's not a huge sample size, and De Paula still has plenty of time to develop with the Dodgers.
He is still the Dodgers' #1 prospect.
In 501 ABs in AA this season, he hit 27 home runs, 37 doubles, and 31 stolen bases.

It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many,” Skubal said. The statement has multiple layers: if
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers future free agent Tarik Skubal, pending his move to the team, joined the celebration of the team’s division win and made an interesting comment about his future.
With champagne pouring and running down his face, Skubal was asked about his outlook on the upcoming postseason push amid the current celebration.
“It’s a ton of fun to celebrate these moments with these guys. It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many,” Skubal said.
The statement has multiple layers: if the Dodgers win more postseason series, they’ll have many more celebrations down the road this year.
The Dodgers will pop bottles at each stop, following the NLDS, NLCS, and the World Series.
However, his lingering free-agent status also hangs in the background of his entire Dodgers tenure. LA is getting a shot to show Skubal what the team and organization can do for him.
Over the offseason, likely before the lockout, Skubal has the chance to sign a deal that keeps the champagne flowing with his “best friend” Blake Snell for years to come.
Odds are, Skubal still isn’t thinking too far ahead; he was speaking about this season, but as the Dodgers keep winning, things are moving in their favor in the Skubal sweepstakes.
Also, this hasn’t stopped fan speculation that the comments mean more.
Dodgers fans think Skubal is staying
“I’m holding on to Skubal saying ‘this is the first of many’ which would lead me to believe he’s gonna resign with the Dodgers!!!,” @PokieNFace said on X.
“He dropped a hint I think,” @topherbutler6 wrote.
“Yea he’s not leaving ?,” @ItsGeorgyBruh added.
“Skubal in La next year,” @YoPr0digy also replied in the comments

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers were already playoff-bound for the 14th straight season. But after taking down the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, they're winners of the NL West for the 13th time in that span and for the fifth season in a row.
Of course, the streak LA cares about most will be at stake in the postseason. The Dodgers are aiming to become the first team to three-peat as World Series champions since the fabled New York Yankees of 1998-2000.
With the victory Thursday, the Dodgers (93-60) have the second-best record in the NL, behind only the Milwaukee Brewers (95-58), who clinched the NL Central earlier this week but dropped their series finale to the Pirates on Thursday. The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Es hora de que Shohei Ohtani renuncie al pitcheo de manera definitiva
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal. A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo. item.content:encoded:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.
Publicado originalmente en www.sportsillustrated.com el 15/09/2026, traducido al español para SI México.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
item.dc:creator: JEFF WALLNER
item.description: Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati. “Es algo muy importante. item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki has been sidelined for the last three weeks due to a lingering blister.
After dealing with the blister during a late-August start, Sasaki was removed from the game and later added to the injured list.
"When I was facing the first hitter in the fourth inning, I actually didn't feel anything coming beforehand," Sasaki said through an interpreter after that game. "My skin just ripped off, and then after that, it got worse. ... I thought I was able to manage at first because the skin was still there, but after that, it kept getting worse, and I think it affected my slider afterwards."
As he has continued to recover and trend back towards the mound, Sasaki threw a simulated game on Wednesday, in which he completed four innings.
The Dodgers were thinking about having Sasaki pitch in Thursday's series finale against the Cincinnati Reds, but instead elected for the sim game, and to have him set up to return next week.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said on Wednesday. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. ... So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
At first, the Dodgers weren't sure if Sasaki would be back in the rotation — where he appeared for 23 starts this season — or if he would head to the bullpen.
However, after Blake Snell exited Wednesday's start after one inning, Roberts confirmed Sasaki would rejoin the rotation for the time being.
Sasaki had a 4.72 ERA across the first eight starts of his MLB career last season before he was placed on the injured list with a shoulder impingement for over four months. Upon his late-September return, he was not placed back into the rotation, but rather into a bullpen role that saw plenty of success.
In his first two innings of work, Sasaki struck out four and allowed just one hit and zero runs. His next appearance came in the postseason.
For the remainder of the postseason — one that included the first three saves of his MLB career, the pivotal 8th through 10th innings of an NLDS thriller and even 2.2 innings in the World Series — Sasaki established a 0.84 ERA across 10.2 innings of work.
Sasaki will likely return to the bullpen for the postseason this year, especially with the question marks surrounding Edwin Díaz. However, for now, he appears set to make one more start, and improve upon his 4.60 ERA over 119.1 innings this season.

Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.content:encoded:
After their win on Thursday afternoon, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West for the 13th time in the past 14 seasons.
LA has a dominant team once again, which is no surprise, especially with two frontline aces on their staff in Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell. While Skubal and Snell haven’t played long together, as Snell was activated off the IL semi-recently and Skubal was traded to LA in August, you can tell the two have formed a close bond while talking shop about pitching.
After the Reds game on Thursday, the Dodgers celebrated in the visiting clubhouse, and Skubal and Sale had a hilarious moment together.
More MLB on Heavy: Mookie Betts Drops Heartfelt Message After Dodgers-Reds Game
Tarik Skubal ‘Little Bros’ Blake Snell
After the game, Tarik Skubal sent this message to Blake Snell:
“This is my best friend. He’s my little brother.”
Tarik Skubal is 29 years old.
Blake Snell is 33 years old.
Perhaps they are best friends, but to say someone four years older than you is hilarious.
However, the joke works because both Skubal and Snell are among the two best starters in all of MLB.
Here was the full exchange:
Skubal: “It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many.”
Snell: “Tell em it’s gonna be special because you’re playing this postseason with your boy.”
Skubal: “This is my best friend; he’s my little brother.”
Blake Snell has been known as a locker room clown since joining the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Former Los Angeles Dodgers Pitcher Suddenly Released by New MLB Team
How Do Blake Snell and Tarik Skubal Impact Dodgers’ Postseason Chances?
The Los Angeles Dodgers will likely capture a top-2 seed in the NL, which grants them a bye into the NLDS.
Who their opponent will be remains TBD, but what is determined is that Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell will be the focal point of the Dodgers’ rotation (along with Yamamoto).
So LA needs the dominant southpaws to be at their best in each start they make.
Easier said than done, yes, but both Skubal and Snell were flat-out unhittable in last season’s postseason, so there’s reason to believe they both carry some October mojo.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Announce 3 Roster Changes Before Phillies Series

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers, like all other 29 MLB teams, have around 10 games left on the schedule.
LA already knows it will be headed to October, but the Dodgers are still aiming to clinch the NL West, which could happen on Thursday afternoon.
As the Dodgers gear up for October, one of the biggest storylines surrounding the team is who will close games out.
Edwin Diaz was signed to be the team's closer, but he's had inconsistency problems. On Thursday, during their series with the Reds, LA revealed its plans with Edwin Diaz.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Positive Shohei Ohtani News During Reds Series
Edwin Diaz to be Activated Off IL on Friday
According to multiple reporters who follow the Los Angeles Dodgers, Edwin Diaz will be activated from the Injured List on Friday.
"Dave Roberts said Edwin Diaz will meet team in Los Angeles. When he is activated it will be "low leverage" situations and will have to earn higher leverage spots."
So, that basically rules out the possibility that Edwin Diaz will be a closer for the Dodgers, which is a good call by Dave Roberts. Despite a few solid outings on paper, it feels like every time Diaz has pitched for the Dodgers this season, there's always been added nerves to the situation.
More MLB on Heavy: Blake Snell's Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
More on Edwin Diaz Injury….
Edwin Diaz has been sidelined since mid-August with a neck injury.
He will be eased into the bullpen fold, and the good news for LA is that they may have already wrapped up the NL West when Diaz joins the team in LA on Friday.
"Díaz signed a three-year, $69MM contract over the winter, but it's been a lost season for the All-Star closer. He's pitched in just 13 2/3 big league innings due to injury and hasn't looked anywhere close to his usual self when healthy enough to take the mound. He's been rocked for 18 runs on 25 hits and 10 walks, leading to an awful 11.85 earned run average. Díaz entered the season with a career 39.9% strikeout rate and 8.6% walk rate. Those marks have plummeted to 24.1% and 12.7% this season, and his average fastball has dropped from 97.2 mph in 2025 to 96.3 mph in 2026."
In other Dodgers news, Andy Pages could be nearing a return as well, and manager Dave Roberts did not rule out a return for Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, which has just a week and a half left.

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
They hit their magic number, but minus the magic.
The Dodgers trudged toward October by clinching their 13th National League West title in 14 years on Thursday, their customary march mired in a quicksand of questions.
Has any Dodger team during this golden era entered the playoffs with more injuries, more uncertainty, and a greater fear of underachievement?
Will the party in Cincinnati be the last time they celebrate this season?
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
The Three-Peat looks like a no-go.
Despite the best efforts from baseball’s best braintrust, their latest creation simply doesn’t have the appearance of a championship team.
They’re aging, they’re hurting and, with only a couple of weeks left until the beginning of their annual autumnal angst, they look tired and taut and unprepared for this monumental tussle with history.
“I think for me, the message was, ‘We haven’t come close to playing our best baseball yet.’” manager Dave Roberts told reporters when relaying his speech to the team earlier this week upon clinching a record-tying 14th consecutive playoff berth.
He added, “The message was, we’ve accomplished a lot up to this point, all the while not playing our best baseball. So let’s get some of these guys healthy.”
Haven’t come close to playing our best baseball… Let’s get some of these guys healthy.
Not exactly “Win one for the Gipper” stuff, but completely accurate. These postseason’s themes are more realistic than inspirational, and for good reason.
No, they haven’t come close to playing their best baseball. Forget what you see in these season-ending games against some of the worst teams. Remember, instead, what they’ve done against some of baseball’s best.
Since the All-Star break, they are 4-12 against the five National League playoff contenders. The Atlanta Braves swept them. The Chicago Cubs swept them. The Milwaukee Brewers dominated them.
These teams will be waiting for them in October, and even baseball’s richest roster might not be enough to carry this staggered bunch through their toughest stretch. They’ve played a lot of games in three years, all under baseball’s brightest spotlight, every night, scores of media, millions of fans, a worldwide whirl for 28 regular dudes, and it’s finally taken its toll.
They’ve hit the wall… and the wall is about to hit back.
“It’s not easy, I think it’s a lot harder than people think it is,” said Roberts. “Human nature alone, when you’re hungry, when you’re chasing something, it’s a lot more easy to be motivated, versus, having been there, done that, it gets a little trite, a little old.”
He added: “To keep guys enthusiastic, focused, hungry, that’s harder. But to their credit, they stayed the course. And for me, we’re just as hungry as we were in ‘24 and ‘25. This is a separate season. Our guys understand.”
The 1988-89 Lakers understood, too. And they still got burned in ways that Dodger fans will find painfully familiar. Showtime was chasing the original “three-peat” trademarked by Pat Riley when the Lakers were swept by the Detroit Pistons in a Finals that seemed cursed,
Byron Scott missed the series with a hamstring injury and Magic Johnson essentially missed the final two games with a hamstring injury and they couldn’t survive.
This looks like the Dodgers today. Their injuries feel too major, and the impact too deep.
Start with Shohei Ohtani. The Dodgers haven’t won a full-season championship in 38 years without him at the top of the lineup. He’ll be there again, but his body has been breaking down for the last couple of months, and, before being recently placed on the injured list — finally! — he was only a shadow of himself.
He hasn’t hit a home run or driven in a run outside of Coors Field in more than a month. In his last 24 games before going on the IL with biceps and knee issues, he was batting .198. The Dodgers can’t admit it, and Ohtani would never acknowledge it, but this is a man in serious need of an extended rest.
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
Also on the injured list in these final days is Andy Pages, who was having a career year before breaking his hand. He’ll return without much time to get ready for October, and this is a man who will need some time, as he has a career .114 average in the postseason and was even benched last year before he redeemed himself with that picturesque catch over Kiké Hernández.
Speaking of last October’s heroes, the biggest savior has also spent the summer in pain, Will Smith battling neck issues until recently returning to the lineup. But the comeback has been bumpy. In his initial games since returning at the start of September, Smith was batting .171. Last October he set a major league record by catching 73 innings in the World Series. He is still paying the price.
Then there’s Freddie Freeman, whose bat doesn’t have the same pop, who’s step doesn’t have the same spring, and who has his worst OPS in 14 years. Add an inconsistent Mookie Betts and an incredibly streaky Teoscar Hernández to an already-shaky lineup.
It’s been such an unsteady year, Andrew Friedman’s two big offseason acquisitions have been busts. Edwin Díaz has been terrible, and then injured, then terrible again. Kyle Tucker has been terrible, then worse, then mostly invisible.
Even the Dodgers two role-playing heroes have seemingly disappeared. Kiké Hernández, at age 35, has his lowest home-run total — three — in 12 years. Miguel Rojas, at age 37, has his lowest home run and RBI totals in nine years.
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
As if they didn’t have enough problems on the field and at the plate, check out the mound. No, don’t.
Even what should be their strength is now being threatened. Blake Snell left Wednesday’s game early with groin issues and Tyler Glasnow recently complained of general discomfort. This leaves a proven playoff rotation of two, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, and if you think Yamamoto threw a lot of innings last October, this time he won’t be able to leave the mound for a month.
In all, this is a Dodger team facing its toughest challenge yet, their quest for an historic three-peat much tougher than the last two journeys, one that will require arguably the greatest stretch of baseball in franchise history to complete.
This division title is a nice beginning.
It could also be the end.

item.dc:creator: TJ French

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers endured a bit of an injury scare regarding starter Blake Snell in their recent game against the Cincinnati Reds.
Snell, who made the start for LA, was pulled after just one inning with groin tightness.
During the game, reports surfaced that the Snell injury was not thought to be serious, and that Snell should still be in line to make his start.
Well, after the end of the game, Snell spoke with the media, and his comments about the injury should give Dodgers fans some assurance.
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
What Did Blake Snell Say About His Groin Injury?
Per @SportsNetLA, here is some of what Blake Snell had to say about his early exit:
"I was gonna try to get through five, but I just knew I didn't have a good shot of doing that and remaining healthy."
He also added that he's "day-to-day", and "should be good" to make his next start.
So while many Dodgers fans may have been panicking after he was pulled from the game, it's expected to be a precautionary measure.
The Dodgers' October rotation would still look very formidable without Blake Snell in it, but considering Snell's additions last October, LA is likely going to be as careful as possible when it comes to him being at a full bill of health in a few weeks.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Critical Roki Sasaki Update During Reds Series
Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dave Roberts: First-round bye would be more ‘beneficial’ than ever for injury-riddled Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now. “I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason. Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch th
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now.
“I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason.
Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch that first-round bye. The Dodgers trail the Milwaukee Brewers by three games for the top seed.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset,” Roberts said. “But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge.”
Blake Snell joined the long list of players with injury concerns when he left his start Wednesday after just one inning due to left groin tightness. The Dodgers also have questions about Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps), Freddie Freeman (knee), Edgardo Henriquez (back), Andy Pages (hand), Roki Sasaki (blister) and Dalton Rushing (elbow).
Pages has been swinging a bat and hitting off the Trajekt machine this week, and it is “very likely” he will be activated from the IL during the homestand starting Friday, according to Roberts.
Ohtani has been “progressing” this week and is feeling “normal-ish” with no pain in his right arm or left knee, Roberts said.
“He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when (his) time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Snell could undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his groin injury. But he was optimistic after the game Wednesday that he had pulled back and left the game soon enough that it won’t be a serious issue and he might be able to make one more start before the end of the regular season.
“It’s all contingent on how he feels and potential imaging,” Roberts said. “It doesn’t make sense to just shut him down until the postseason if he can pitch. But again, if he’s not 100 percent to pitch, then we have no problem kicking the can.”
DIAZ RETURN
Right-hander Edwin Diaz completed his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday and will join the Dodgers in Los Angeles this weekend with the expectation that he will be activated from the Injured List.
Diaz will be used in “low-leverage” situations, Roberts said, with a need to prove he can pitch well enough to assume a bigger role if he is on the postseason roster.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Roberts called Diaz’s final outing with OKC was “his best one yet.” Diaz pitched a scoreless inning, gave up a double and didn’t get a single swing-and-miss on any of 15 pitches.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said of what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA), Friday, 7:10 p.m., Apple TV, 570 AM

This is your one-stop shop for every Dodgers stint on the injured list during the 2026 season. We’ll also include every time a player misses time on the paternity list, bereavement leave, or is on the family medical emergency list as well.
Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we’ll note it here.
During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list, some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024, while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL.
Every injured-list stint is a transaction and will also be chronicled on our 40-man roster page. Both are essentially living documents that will be constantly updated throughout the season as these moves happen.
Injured-list stints for pitchers are a minimum of 15 days, and for position players it’s at least 10 days.
During spring training, the Dodgers placed both Evan Phillips and Kiké Hernández on the 60-day injured list, which opened up space on the 40-man roster for other moves. On opening day, six more Dodgers were placed on the injured list, including Blake Snell and Tommy Edman.

item.title: [The New York Times] Shohei Ohtani’s feeling ‘normal…ish’ as Dodgers sort out health issues before playoffs
item.dc:creator: Fabian Ardaya

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers have kept open the possibility that Shohei Ohtani will return before the end of the regular season, though they are up against a running clock.
Any progress is good progress for the Dodgers’ most important piece, so it was a good thing when Ohtani started up activity Tuesday and Thursday and didn’t report any discomfort in his bothersome biceps, balky left knee and tight neck.
“Feels normal…ish,” manager Dave Roberts said Thursday morning.
Advertisement
Ohtani went on the injured list late last week, ending a months-long injury saga and giving him a maximum of five additional regular season games to play in before another the playoffs. He is eligible to return as soon as Sept. 23, though Roberts did not commit to that timeline.
There are still steps for Ohtani to take. He swung off a tee on Tuesday, had Wednesday off from baseball activity and could hit off a coach’s pitching by the end of the week. He will need to face some sort of live pitching before he appears in a game and even then, the maximum of five games does not feel like a lot for him to get his timing right.
Especially since, given how the Dodgers tried kicking the can on shelving Ohtani, he will return after having taken just four plate appearances since Sept. 2. Ohtani, clearly compromised by his nagging injuries, had just six hits over his final 49 at-bats before hitting the IL.
They still need Ohtani, even if he is not 100 percent. The oldest lineup in baseball has shown its age. Even if Ohtani’s role on the postseason roster is simply to provide the threat of launching a ball into the seats, that is valuable in their quest for a third consecutive World Series title. The Dodgers’ first road trip without Ohtani since his arrival in 2024 has been noticeably different.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yoshinobu Yamamoto joked through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. Yamamoto has instead had to rely on Roki Sasaki, “but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Díaz’ place in the bullpen
Edwin Díaz will return to the Dodgers on Friday, but not as the club’s closer. Nothing is guaranteed for the guy the Dodgers gave $69 million to solve their ninth-inning problem and who now could be on the bubble for the postseason roster thanks to his 11.85 ERA.
Díaz, who has made only 16 major-league appearances thanks to arthroscopic elbow surgery and a later neck issue, has also pitched poorly in rehab. A five-run blowup on Sunday with Triple-A Oklahoma City caused the Dodgers to delay Díaz’s return. But a scoreless inning on Wednesday — albeit one in which Díaz gave up a 104 mph double and did not induce a single swing-and-miss — was enough for the Dodgers to bring him back to the big leagues.
“It was his best one yet,” Roberts said of Díaz, whose has a low bar to clear.
Advertisement
Díaz will return in lower-leverage situations and have to show prove over the final week of the regular season he deserves a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen, even if their list of right-handed relief options is thinning.
“I think like anything it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities but then you also got to perform, right?”
Edgardo Henriquez was the club’s most trusted reliever before he went on the injured list on Monday. Subsequent imaging showed what Roberts dubbed a “low-grade” back strain, and the manager said he was “hopeful” that Henriquez could still be a postseason option.
Another potential solution, Sasaki, is now needed in the rotation after Blake Snell exited Wednesday’s start with left groin tightness. The Dodgers will know more about Snell’s fate once they return to Los Angeles and potentially get imaging done, but Sasaki is currently slated to pitch at some point next week against the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers have also been cagey about Tyler Glasnow’s status. Roberts was vague after Glasnow’s last start, but said the right-hander “didn’t feel great” going into it. The Dodgers sent Glasnow directly to Los Angeles afterwards rather than have him travel with the club to Cincinnati, and Roberts said Glasnow’s preparation for Friday’s start has otherwise been normal.
Pages’ return imminent
Andy Pages will “very likely” return to the Dodgers’ lineup without playing in rehab games at some point during the six-game home stand that opens Friday. Pages has progressed quickly from left hand fracture and the Dodgers are banking on the All-Star’s defensive value in center field despite the chances he’ll struggle on offensive.
Pages moved from hitting softer baseballs to hitting normal ones this week and will hit off the Trajekt Arc machine to simulate live at-bats. There aren’t a lot of games to go around on a rehab assignment, anyway, though Oklahoma City did clinch a postseason berth on Wednesday (those games start next week).

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers latest injury crisis throws Roki Sasaki usage plan in flux

All year, it seemed clear that Sasaki was destined to wind up back in the Dodgers bullpen, reprising the late-inning leverage role he unexpectedly ascended to as a rookie last October. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– Even after watching Roki Sasaki complete the final checkmark in his recovery from a blister on Wednesday afternoon, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts couldn’t say for sure how the team would use the 24-year-old phenom pitcher.
All year, it seemed clear that Sasaki was destined to wind up back in the Dodgers bullpen, reprising the late-inning leverage role he unexpectedly ascended to as a rookie last October.
Though he had turned a corner as a starter during the second half of this campaign, posting a 2.31 ERA in his first six outings after the All-Star break, he had still long looked like a superfluous piece of the Dodgers’ rotation, an excess arm stuck behind the four veteran superstars the club had penciled in to lead this fall’s World Series push.
However, Roberts remained non-committal about Sasaki’s plan on Wednesday, after the right-hander completed a four-inning, 48-pitch session of live batting practice in Cincinnati, in what was hoped to be his final step before returning from the injured list.
On the one hand, the skipper noted, the Dodgers could shift Sasaki to the bullpen now, give him time to re-acclimate to relief duties, and let him focus on just short-burst stints.
But on the other, “one can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts countered. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Hours later, the something Roberts was worried about might have suddenly happened –– with Blake Snell’s groin injury having direct repercussions on Sasaki’s potential task.
In Wednesday night’s game, Snell left his start after just one inning because of left groin tightness. While he’s hopeful he avoided any serious injury, he has had bouts of groin issues in the past that have sidelined him for up to a month at a time.
If that were to be the case again now, Sasaki would be first in line to replace Snell in the Dodgers’ postseason rotation.
Mix in the uncertainty surrounding fellow starter Tyler Glasnow faced following his four-inning outing last weekend in Miami –– after which he conspicuously returned immediately to Los Angeles to limit extra travel on the rest of this road trip –– and Sasaki now seems like a valuable starting-pitching insurance policy the Dodgers might still need to utilize in the playoffs.
That’s why, by the end of Wednesday’s game, Roberts was able to at least be definitive about the team’s plan for Sasaki when he comes off the injured list, confirming he is likely to make a start sometime next week, perhaps during a visit from the San Diego Padres.
In a best-case scenario, that will be Sasaki’s last time starting a game this year, with an otherwise healthy rotation allowing the Dodgers to shift him to an equally banged-up bullpen.
But for now, the team can’t be certain of anything.
Which means, when it comes to Sasaki, all options remain on the table.
