item.content:encoded:
Blake Snell exits Dodgers’ loss early because of injury
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — The trouble started as Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell threw in the Great American Ball Park bullpen before the game.
“I felt good all day, and then the second-to-last pitch of the bullpen, I threw a slider and then I felt it grab,” Snell said of the groin tightness that ended up taking him out of the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds early. “So I was like, ‘Alright, let’s see what we can do.’”
With Snell guiding the ball without driving hard off his back leg, his velocity was down a tick or two through a 19-pitch first inning. He gave up one hit, a single to Sal Stewart, which he quickly erased with a successful pick-off that caught Stewart in an inning-ending run-down.
“I was going to try to get through five [innings],” he said, “but I just knew I didn’t really have a good shot at doing that and remaining healthy.”
In a conversation with manager Dave Roberts, pitching coach Mark Prior and head athletic trainer Thomas Albert, they all agreed the best course of action would be to pull Snell from the game. Right-handed reliever Blake Treinen replaced him in the second inning.
With only 10 games left in the season, it’s unclear when Snell will be ready to pitch again.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
The Dodgers’ loss marked Snell’s eighth start of the season. His 2026 debut was delayed by shoulder fatigue. And then after one start, he landed back on the injured list to undergo arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow.
Since returning, he hasn’t given up more than one run in a start. Through Wednesday, Snell has a 1.86 ERA. And he’s a key member of the Dodgers’ projected postseason rotation.
“I don’t think anyone can sit here right now and say what’s going to happen in the next week to 10 days,” Roberts said, noting that the team would decide whether to send him to get imaging after they returned to Los Angeles. “It’s under the, ‘I’m glad it’s not worse and we caught it early’ [category].”
Snell has a history of left groin and adductor strains. He spent time on the IL in 2021, 2022 and 2024 for such injuries. He said this injury didn’t feel nearly as severe as any of those.
“[In the past] I felt like that and then I kept pitching on two of them and strained both of them,” he said. “One was a grade one, one was a grade two. So I’m definitely happy I stopped. … I’m aware if I kept pitching, I definitely would’ve strained it. So for me to stop, that’s a first. Maybe I’m growing up. I don’t know. But that was definitely the right move. And next couple days, we’ll see where we’re at and go from there. But I think I’ll be good to go.”
The last couple years, in an effort to avoid another groin strain, Snell has incorporated Copenhagen planks into his routine, strengthening the area.
“I thought I had this thing figured out,” Snell said. “Well, technically, I still do. I didn’t strain it, so that was a good thing. … I haven’t felt it at all until that pitch in the bullpen, and I was just kind of thrown off by it. So I’ve done what I’ve needed to do to be strong and healthy. Definitely a shock to me.”
After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (groin) removed from start after 1st inning
By Field Level Media
Sep 17 (Field Level Media) – Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell was removed from Wednesday’s game in Cincinnati after one inning and replaced with reliever Blake Treinen.
The Dodgers announced that Snell left the game due to left groin tightness.
Snell struck out Dane Myers to open the bottom of the first and Elly De La Cruz lined out to center before Sal Stewart singled to left. It was the first hit Snell had allowed at Great American Ball Park since he threw a no-hitter there on Aug. 2, 2024, in a 3-0 win for the San Francisco Giants.
The left-hander then caught Stewart leaning from first base and the Reds’ runner was caught stealing to end the first inning. Treinen came on to replace Snell to start the second.
Snell had arthroscopic surgery in May to remove loose bodies in his left elbow and returned in August. He has been one of the hottest pitchers in baseball since, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA with 46 strikeouts in his last six starts entering Wednesday.
(–Field Level Media)

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Now what?
Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in four simulated innings to Dodgers hitters on Wednesday afternoon, testing the blister on his right hand that landed him on the injured list. He gave up a home run to Eliezer Alfonzo but otherwise “was good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Sasaki threw with Dermabond on his injured finger. A surgical adhesive used to close cuts and incisions, pitchers are allowed to use it in games if their team gets permission from MLB in advance.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. What does it look like as we sit here on the 17th or 18th of September, whatever? So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
Sasaki seemed destined for a bullpen role again this postseason, a role he assumed successfully last year. But the Dodgers have reason to hesitate on turning Sasaki into a reliever with Blake Snell leaving his start after just one inning on Wednesday night and Tyler Glasnow’s status.
Glasnow flew back to Los Angeles after his start in Miami. It was the second consecutive start in which Glasnow was not sharp and this time he could be seen in the dugout stretching out his back. But after the game, he said his back felt fine and Roberts said Glasnow threw a “normal” bullpen session in L.A. on Wednesday and is scheduled to make his next start on Friday night.
Sasaki is penciled in now to start during the series against the San Diego Padres in Los Angeles next week and remain a starter at least for now.
“One can argue it’s best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up, because if something does happen, he’s built up,” Roberts said. “The other side is you can assimilate him into the ’pen and get comfortable in that role – if that is the role.
“But again, I don’t want to speak out of turn and say that’s done, because it’s not.”
NO SHO
The Dodgers are about to complete their first road trip in three seasons without Shohei Ohtani. Yoshinobu Yamamoto might have missed Ohtani more than any other of his teammates.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yamamoto joked through his interpreter when asked about Ohtani’s absence. “All I have is Roki, but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Back in Los Angeles, Ohtani has been receiving treatment for his knee and bicep injuries. According to Roberts, Ohtani began swinging a bat, hitting off a tee this week.
“There’s going to be a consistent build-up,” Roberts said. “Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”
Ohtani will be eligible to be activated from the IL next Wednesday. Whether he is ready to play that day or shortly after, Roberts said the expectation is that Ohtani will return in time to play before the regular season ends on Sept. 27.
“I do,” Roberts said. “Whether it happens or not is to be determined. But I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games. Don’t know how many of them.”
COMING/GOING
Right-hander Edwin Diaz made his fifth rehab appearance with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless inning to close out the Comets’ playoff berth-clinching victory. Diaz did allow a double to a fellow big-leaguer on rehab, Miguel Andujar.
Meanwhile, Edgardo Henriquez returned to Los Angeles and underwent an MRI, which confirmed the diagnosis of a “low-grade back strain,” Roberts said. He won’t be eligible to pitch again in the regular season but Roberts said the Dodgers are “hopeful” he could come back for the postseason.
Left-hander Kris Bubic was activated from the 60-day IL before Wednesday’s game and right-hander Paul Gervase was returned to OKC. In order to clear a spot on the 40-man roster for Bubic, Triple-A outfielder Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Right-hander Landon Knack will be added to the active roster before Thursday’s game and Bobby Miller will be returned to OKC.
ALSO
Outfield prospect Charles Davalan (the 41st pick in last year’s draft) was named MVP of the Class-A Midwest League and Great Lakes manager Jair Fernandez was named the league’s Manager of the Year. Davalan hit .292 with 24 home runs and a .937 OPS. He is scheduled to play in the Arizona Fall League, where he is expected to start testing out a possible conversion to second base.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Justin Wrobleski, 11-5, 3.78 ERA) at Reds (RHP Brady Singer, 6-14, 5.38 ERA), Thursday, 9:40 a.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Elly De La Cruz conectó un jonrón de dos carreras y los Rojos de Cincinnati, al menos de manera temporal, evitaron que los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraran el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria por 6-2 la noche del miércoles.
Los Dodgers (92-60) necesitaban ganar o que San Diego perdiera para conquistar su quinta corona divisional consecutiva y la 13ra en 14 temporadas. Los Padres jugaban en Colorado más tarde el miércoles.
El zurdo Blake Snell abrió por los Dodgers, pero salió del juego después de una entrada por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Snell, quien lanzó un juego sin hits con los Gigantes en su última aparición en el Great American Ball Park, enfrentó a tres bateadores, permitió un imparable y ponchó a uno en 19 lanzamientos.
Blake Treinen tomó el relevo en la segunda entrada como el primero de seis relevistas utilizados por Los Ángeles.
Mookie Betts conectó un sencillo ante Andrew Abbott en la tercera y anotó con un doble de Will Smith para poner a los Dodgers arriba 1-0. Abbott permitió una carrera con tres hits y otorgó cinco bases por bolas en 4 2/3 entradas. Tejay Antone (3-2), el tercero de seis lanzadores de Cincinnati, consiguió el último out de la sexta.
El jonrón del dominicano De La Cruz ante Seth Halvorsen (1-2), su 28vo de la temporada, puso a los Rojos al frente 2-1 en la tercera. Fue el quinto cuadrangular de De La Cruz contra los Dodgers esta temporada, la mayor cantidad de cualquier jugador rival.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI (AP) — Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run homer and the Cincinnati Reds at least temporarily prevented the Los Angeles Dodgers from clinching the NL West title with a 6-2 victory on Wednesday night.
The Dodgers (92-60) needed a win or a loss by San Diego to win their fifth straight NL West crown and 13th in 14 seasons. The Padres played at Colorado later Wednesday.
Left-hander Blake Snell started for the Dodgers but departed after one inning with left groin tightness. Snell, who threw a no-hitter for the Giants in his last appearance in Great American Ball Park, faced three batters, allowing a hit with a strikeout on 19 pitches.
Blake Treinen took over in the second as the first of six relievers used by Los Angeles.
Mookie Betts singled off Andrew Abbott in the third and scored on Will Smith's double to put the Dodgers ahead 1-0. Abbott allowed a run on three hits with five walks in 4 2/3 innings. Tejay Antone (3-2), the third of six Cincinnati pitchers, got the last out of the sixth.
De La Cruz's homer off Seth Halvorsen (1-2), his 28th of the season, put the Reds ahead 2-1 in the third. It was De La Cruz's fifth longball against the Dodgers this season, most of any opposing player.
Dane Myers' homer off Bobby Miller, his seventh, extended the Reds' lead to 3-1 in the fifth.
Juan Brito's RBI single made it 4-2 in the sixth.
TJ Friedl singled with the bases loaded in the seventh to drive in two runs. Sal Stewart was thrown out at the plate by Dodgers center fielder Tommy Edman to end the inning.
The Dodgers stranded 12 runners and went 0 for 11 with runners in scoring position.
Up next
RHP Brady Singer (6-14, 5.38 ERA) will start Thursday's series finale for the Reds. The Dodgers had not announced their starter.

item.title: [New York Post] Blake Snell departs early and Dodgers’ rotation suddenly a question mark
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Shohei Ohtani’s aching right arm. Freddie Freeman’s throbbing right knee. Edwin Díaz’s disastrous form on a minor-league rehabilitation assignment. Whatever problems surfaced in recent weeks, the Dodgers were able to convince themselves they could overcome them. The reason: Even with Ohtani unable to pitch, they had the most talented starting rotation of this era. Suddenly, that source of comfort is a major concern. Blake Snell departed his start in Cincinnati on Wednesday after just one inning
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani’s aching right arm. Freddie Freeman’s throbbing right knee. Edwin Díaz’s disastrous form on a minor-league rehabilitation assignment.
Whatever problems surfaced in recent weeks, the Dodgers were able to convince themselves they could overcome them.
The reason: Even with Ohtani unable to pitch, they had the most talented starting rotation of this era.
Suddenly, that source of comfort is a major concern.
Blake Snell departed his start in Cincinnati on Wednesday after just one inning with what was described as a tight left groin.
Consider that Tyler Glasnow traveled directly home from Miami rather than to follow the Dodgers to Great American Ball Park for their four-game series against the Reds, and there are reasons to be worried.
Very worried.
With an inconsistent offense and combustible bullpen, the Dodgers were going to be heavily dependent on their starting pitching in the playoffs.
That rotation could now be unraveling.

The last time Snell strained his left groin was when he was pitching for the San Francisco Giants in 2024. He was sidelined for a month.
For what it’s worth, Snell is convinced this particular injury isn’t severe and plans to make his next start, according to people familiar with this situation.
“Stopped before it got too bad,” one of the people said.
Then again, weren’t similar claims once made about Ohtani?
As for Glasnow, he remains on track to pitch on Friday.
Manager Dave Roberts said Glasnow skipped the Cincinnati leg of the trip to better prepare for his starting assignment at Dodger Stadium against the San Francisco Giants.
“Get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time,” Roberts said.
By sending Glasnow back to Los Angeles, the Dodgers spared him a three-hour flight from Miami to Cincinnati.
Glasnow was sidelined for 3 ½ months because of back problems, and Roberts intimated something could be wrong with him after his most recent start. In his last two appearances, the 6-foot-8 right-hander gave up a combined eight runs, 11 hits and seven walks in 10 innings.
The questions about Snell’s and Glasnow’s health came at a time when the rotation was coming together before the postseason.
Snell in particular was sharp after returning from an elbow cleanup that cost him three months. Before his early departure on Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 earned-run average since he was activated from the injured list on Aug. 11.
Snell wasn’t the only Cy Young Award-caliber pitcher rounding into shape.
The day before Snell scaled the mound, it was Yamamoto’s turn to do so, and last year’s World Series Most Valuable Player pitched seven scoreless innings in a 4-0 win over the Reds.
The seven-inning start was the third in a row for Yamamoto, who improved his record to 14-8 and lowered his earned-run average to 2.51.
“I feel really good and I don’t have any physical problems,” Yamamoto told reporters in Japanese. “I want to treat practice each and every day with importance and go into October in the best condition.”
The opening game of the series was started by Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the trade deadline.
Skubal pitched seven scoreless innings of his own in a 4-1 victory over the Reds. In his previous start, which was also against the Reds but at Dodger Stadium, Skubal pitched 7 ⅓ innings.
“Just getting in a rhythm,” Skubal said.
Just last week, the Dodgers had a playoff rotation that would have looked to other teams like the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
Now, there’s a chance they could be forced to send Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan to the mound in playoff games.
The Dodgers could conceivably win a championship with a rotation of Yamamoto, Skubal, Sasaki and Sheehan but that would require their offense to be productive.
How much can the Dodgers count on that, considering the physical problems Ohtani and Freeman have encountered? And how would using Sasaki as a starter instead of a reliever affect their bullpen?
Snell removed himself from his start on Wednesday so the Dodgers wouldn’t have to find out. The question is whether he did so in time. Their season depends on it.

item.content:encoded:
Solo lanza una entrada
Blake Snell sale con molestias en la ingle
CINCINNATI, MLB.com -- El lanzador zurdo Blake Snell abandonó su apertura contra los Rojos debido a una molestia en la ingle izquierda después de lanzar solo una entrada el miércoles por la noche en el Great American Ball Park.
Snell ya sufrió una lesión similar en el pasado, perdiéndose algunos partidos en 2024 cuando jugaba con los Giants .
El lanzador diestro Blake Treinen comenzó a calentar en la parte alta de la segunda entrada y relevó a Snell en la parte baja de la misma.
Snell lanzó 19 pitcheos enfrentándose al mínimo de bateadores en la primera entrada, permitiendo un sencillo con dos outs a Sal Stewart antes de ser eliminado en un intento de robo de base. Snell lanzó ocho rectas de cuatro costuras con una velocidad promedio de 94.5 mph, 1.5 mph menos que su promedio de la temporada.
Esta temporada, Snell ha estado en la lista de lesionados dos veces. Al comienzo del año, una fatiga en el hombro izquierdo lo dejó fuera de juego, y después de un partido, volvió a la lista de lesionados por fragmentos sueltos en el codo izquierdo, que fueron extirpados quirúrgicamente. Desde su regreso de la lista de lesionados el 11 de agosto, había tenido un desempeño dominante, con un récord de 4-0 y una efectividad de 1.04 en seis aperturas hasta el miércoles.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- El zurdo Blake Snell abandonó su apertura contra los Rojos debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, luego de lanzar apenas un inning en la derrota por 6-2 la noche del miércoles en el Great American Ball Park.
Snell tiene antecedentes de problemas similares. En 2024, cuando estaba con los Gigantes, ingresó dos veces a la lista de lesionados debido a una distensión en la ingle izquierda y otra en el aductor izquierdo. Antes de eso, también perdió tiempo de juego por lesiones en el aductor en 2021 y 2022.
El derecho Blake Treinen comenzó a calentar en la parte alta del segundo inning y relevó a Snell en la parte baja del episodio. Eso obligó a los Dodgers a recurrir de manera inesperada a un juego de bullpen, utilizando a seis relevistas un día antes de que tuvieran previsto emplear esa misma estrategia en el último encuentro de la serie en Cincinnati el jueves.
Los Dodgers llegaron al miércoles necesitando una victoria sobre los Rojos o una derrota de los Padres en Colorado para conquistar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en los últimos 14 años. Tras la derrota, tendrán dos cosas que seguir de cerca durante el resto de la noche: el resultado de San Diego y el estado de Snell.
Snell realizó 19 pitcheos y enfrentó al mínimo de bateadores en el primer inning. Permitió un sencillo de Sal Stewart con dos outs, pero el novato fue puesto fuera posteriormente en una jugada de viraje e intento de robo. Snell lanzó ocho rectas de cuatro costuras con una velocidad promedio de 94.5 mph, 1.5 mph por debajo de su promedio de la temporada.
Esta temporada, Snell ha estado dos veces en la lista de lesionados. Comenzó el año fuera de acción por fatiga en el hombro izquierdo y regresó a la lista de lesionados después de una apertura debido a cuerpos libres en el codo izquierdo, que fueron retirados quirúrgicamente.
Snell había estado dominante desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados el 11 de agosto, con marca de 4-0 y efectividad de 1.04 en seis aperturas antes del miércoles. No permitió más de una carrera en ninguna de esas salidas y los Dodgers ganaron todas menos una. Su ausencia se hizo sentir cuando el bullpen tuvo que encargarse de los últimos siete innings, con Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller y Jack Dreyer permitiendo dos carreras cada uno.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki presents good playoff problem for Dave Roberts appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
After being pulled from the Los Angeles Dodgers' rotation after suffering a blister on his throwing hand, Roki Sasaki has been working his way back to full strength.
Scheduled to throw a four-inning simulated live session on Wednesday instead of a normal start against the Cincinnati Reds, The California Post's Jack Harris reported that Sasaki performed well, to the point where Dave Roberts and company will have to have discussions about how best to use the second-year flame thrower when the postseason rolls around.
"Roki Sasaki's four-inning/48-pitch live session today went well, per Dave Roberts," Harris wrote. "The team is gonna huddle up now and decide if he will return as a starter or reliever. His likely playoff role is in 'pen, but he's also their best rotation insurance in case of any late injuries too."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
On one hand, Sasaki proved in 2025 that he can be a really good option out of the bullpen, where he finished multiple games for the Dodgers as a closer last October. With Edgardo Henriquez placed on IL as he tries to get healthy enough to make the playoff roster, the Dodgers really don't have an elite right-handed arm in their bullpen and could use one situationally alongside stalwart arms like Alex Vesia, Jack Dreyer, and Tanner Scott.
And yet, as LA fans know all too well, things can change in a hurry, and if injuries start stacking up once more, keeping Sasaki ready to go long might not be the worst idea either, just in case.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI – On a night when the Los Angeles Dodgers could clinch the National League West, they suddenly could have a major issue after two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell exited after one inning and 19 pitches.
The Dodgers said Snell exited with left groin tightness, an area that sent Snell to the injured list in 2021, 2022 and 2024 while with the San Diego Padres and San Francisco Giants. The left-hander has taken precautions ever since in managing that part of his body, often wearing a wrap around his left leg on start days and for bullpen sessions.
Advertisement
He did not throw a pitch harder than 95.9 mph Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds, which is below his season average of 96 mph.
Snell missed the start of the 2026 season because of lingering shoulder fatigue that had plagued him through 2025 and into last year’s World Series run. After making one brief start in May, he underwent the new “NanoNeedle” procedure to remove loose bodies from his left pitching elbow.
He has looked like his Cy Young-winning self since returning Aug. 11, allowing just four runs in 34 2/3 innings (1.04 ERA) in his six starts leading into Wednesday. Snell faced three batters in the first, working around a Sal Stewart single by picking him off successfully to end the first inning.
Blake Treinen quickly warmed up between innings and entered in Snell’s place, suddenly raising some concerns for a team that will be built around its starting pitching in October with a rotation of Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow.
This story will be updated.

item.content:encoded:
Snell has a history of similar issues, twice going on the injured list with a left groin strain and a left adductor strain in 2024 when he was with the Giants. Before that, he also missed time with adductor injuries in '21 and '22.
Right-hander Blake Treinen began warming up in the top of the second inning and relieved Snell in the bottom half of the frame. It became an unscheduled bullpen game, with the Dodgers using six relievers the day before they had been planning to run a bullpen game in Thursday's finale in Cincinnati.
The Dodgers entered Wednesday needing either a win over the Reds or a Padres loss in Colorado to clinch their 13th NL West title in the past 14 years. After their loss, they'll have two things to monitor for the remainder of the evening: San Diego's outcome and Snell's status.
Snell threw 19 pitches while facing the minimum in the first inning, giving up a two-out single to Sal Stewart before the rookie was erased on a pickoff-caught stealing. Snell threw eight four-seamers with an average velocity of 94.5 mph, down 1.5 mph from his season average.
This season, Snell has been on the injured list twice. He was sidelined by left shoulder fatigue to open the year and landed back on the IL after one start with loose bodies in his left elbow, which were surgically removed.
Snell had been dominant since returning from the IL on Aug. 11, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts entering Wednesday. He allowed no more than one run in each of those starts, and the Dodgers won all but one of them. His absence was felt when the bullpen had to cover the final seven innings, with Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller and Jack Dreyer allowing two runs apiece.

The Dodgers were hit by the injury bug again, as left-hander Blake Snell left Wednesday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds early due to left groin tightness.
Snell completed a scoreless first inning, facing the minimum after picking off first baseman Sal Stewart following his two-out single. item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers suffer another injury blow as Blake Snell exits with groin issue
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: CINCINNATI –– For all their other problems lately, the Dodgers could at least cling to the fact that the heart of their starting rotation was healthy. On Wednesday night, that might have suddenly changed. After just one inning and 19 pitches at Great American Ball Park against the Cincinnati Reds, left-hander Blake Snell left his start early with left groin tightness, according to the team, getting surprisingly replaced by reliever Blake Treinen at the beginning of the second. It was not immedia
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– For all their other problems lately, the Dodgers could at least cling to the fact that the heart of their starting rotation was healthy.
On Wednesday night, that might have suddenly changed.
After just one inning and 19 pitches at Great American Ball Park against the Cincinnati Reds, left-hander Blake Snell left his start early with left groin tightness, according to the team, getting surprisingly replaced by reliever Blake Treinen at the beginning of the second.
It was not immediately clear what caused the issue, or how severe his injury was believed to be. However, one source with knowledge of the situation described Snell’s removal as “precautionary,” offering at least some early optimism that he had avoided something more serious.
Still, any concern with Snell represents a huge blow to the Dodgers, who have been resting their World Series three-peat hopes, first and foremost, on the strength of a starting rotation led by Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow.
Lately, Snell had been perhaps the stoutest of that bunch, allowing just four runs over six starts since returning from a surgical procedure in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow.
Of note: Snell was pitching on just four days’ rest Wednesday, the first time he had done that all year.
Injuries have been a recurring problem for Snell since he joined the Dodgers on a five-year, $182 million contract two offseasons ago.
He missed much of last year with a shoulder problem, though was healthy enough in the playoffs to make six outings with a 3.18 ERA en route to the club’s World Series title.
Ongoing shoulder issues sidelined him at the start of this year, before his elbow injury popped up after his first start back in early May.
Snell has had left groin injuries before. He missed more than a month in 2024 when he strained his groin while playing for the San Francisco Giants, and was out the final three weeks of the season in 2021 with an adductor groin strain with the San Diego Padres.
If he faces a similar timeline to return again now, it could put his availability for the start of the playoffs in jeopardy.
Just like that, the Dodgers injury headache has gotten that much worse.

At the conclusion of the first inning, Snell went down to the clubhouse alongside team trainer Thomas
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell has exited Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after one inning in a concerning development with less than two weeks to go in the regular season.
Snell pitched a scoreless first inning with one strikeout across 19 pitches. There didn't appear to be anything noticeably wrong with him during the frame, but his fastball velocity was down.
At the conclusion of the first inning, Snell went down to the clubhouse alongside team trainer Thomas Albert.
Now, he's out of the game, with right-hander Blake Treinen replacing him in the bottom of the second inning.
What is Blake Snell's Injury?
The Dodgers announced Snell was removed from the game with left groin tightness.
Manager Dave Roberts will provide a more substantial update after the game, which will include whether or not Snell will need to go on the injured list.
Dodgers Can't Afford a Blake Snell Injury Right Now
Snell opened the year on the IL as he recovered from shoulder inflammation that dated back to last year. He returned for one start in May before going right back on the IL to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
He missed another three months before returning in August, and has been absolutely dominant ever since.
Entering Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts since coming off the IL. Including Wednesday's scoreless first inning, he has 47 strikeouts over 35.2 innings and hasn't allowed a home run in that stretch.
The Dodgers are relying on Snell and fellow superstar pitchers Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal to carry them in October. Thus, the team will hope Snell isn't dealing with anything serious moving forward.
Who Will Replace Blake Snell in Dodgers Rotation if He's Forced to Miss Time?
The Dodgers' starting rotation is dealing with an onslaught of injury concerns as the season winds down.
While the rotation is led by Yamamoto and Skubal (who underwent midseason elbow surgery while with the Detroit Tigers), behind them is a bunch of question marks.
Tyler Glasnow has struggled since returning from a nearly four-month absence due to a back injury. Justin Wrobleski has been removed from the rotation amid his forearm injury and struggles. Roki Sasaki is currently on the IL with a blister. Eric Lauer is out for the season due to an elbow injury.
Then there's Shohei Ohtani, who won't return as a pitcher this year (and may not even be 100% as a hitter).
The Dodgers recently demoted Emmet Sheehan, but could recall him if Snell goes on the IL. He was sharp over his two September starts, allowing one run over 11.2 innings.
If Snell isn't forced to miss time, the Dodgers will take a big sigh of relief knowing their superstar trio in the starting rotation is intact with October looming. If he's forced to go on the IL, though, it will be yet another massive blow in the team's chances to three-peat.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki's 'last check mark' revealed amid injury recovery appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently in the stretch run of the regular season as they prepare for the MLB playoffs, which are set to get underway in a couple of weeks. The Dodgers appear likely to be the number two team in the NL behind the Milwaukee Brewers, who also finished first in the league last year.
The Dodgers have played recently without pitcher Roki Sasaki, who is on the 15-day injured list with a finger issue.
Now, the team has gotten a positive update on his status moving forward.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Roki Sasaki is throwing a live BP in Cincinnati today. Dodgers are hoping this will be the last check mark in his recovery from a blister. TBD if they'll put him back in rotation or shift him to the bullpen once he's activated," reported Jack Harris of the California Post on X, formerly Twitter.
Sasaki is one of several stars on the Dodgers' pitching staff, one that turned up the heat at just the right time last season en route to their second straight World Series championship.
Injuries have once again played a big role for the Dodgers this season, with Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and reigning league MVP Shohei Ohtani all missing extensive time with various issues, but Los Angeles once again seems to be getting healthy at the right time with the playoffs approaching.
Last year, the Dodgers had no problem going on the road and dispatching the Brewers in the playoffs, something they might have to do once again this time around if the two teams match up again, as many expect them to in the NLCS.
In the meantime, the Dodgers will next hit the field on Wednesday vs the Cincinnati Reds.
Related: Roki Sasaki presents good playoff problem for Dave Roberts' Dodgers
Related: Dodgers make official Kris Bubic roster move before Reds game

item.content:encoded:
Max Muncy is out of the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup for Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds, and the move didn't come as a surprise. Dave Roberts already said as much a day earlier.
The Dodgers manager told reporters Tuesday night that Muncy, infielder Alex Freeland, and outfielder Josue De Paula weren't expected to start Wednesday, according to DodgerBlue on X.com.
The reasoning behind the move is that Andrew Abbott is scheduled to start for the Reds, a lefty with a 6-11 record and a 4.78 ERA this season. All three batters are left-handed hitters who have struggled against left-handed pitching.
We will probably have to remind everyone tomorrow, but Dave Roberts already said Max Muncy, Alex Freeland and Josue De Paula aren’t expected to be in the lineup.
— Dodger Blue (@DodgerBlue1958) September 16, 2026
Muncy has hit .222 against left-handed pitching over his career, compared to .235 against right-handers. Ironically, this season, Muncy has hit better against pitching from the left side, batting .257 with six home runs and 15 RBIs versus .249 with 22 homers and 56 RBIs against the right side.
Those numbers have shaped how Roberts has deployed Muncy late in games and against certain matchups. The 36-year-old is in the middle of a bounce-back year that included his third career All-Star selection, his first since 2021.
The Dodgers enter Wednesday's game with a 92-59 record and a 10-game lead over the San Diego Padres in the National League West, needing just one more win or a Padres loss to clinch the division. The Dodgers have already locked up a playoff berth for the 14th straight season, tying the major league record with the Atlanta Braves.
While the Dodgers will be without left-handed bats, Roberts will lean on left-hander Blake Snell on the mound, giving the Dodgers the best possible matchup to attack Abbott without their top left-handed bats.

A return to the active roster appears imminent, though the Dodgers haven’t decided wh
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers moved closer to restoring their pitching depth before Wednesday’s series finale against the Cincinnati Reds.
Right-handed starter Roki Sasaki threw a live batting practice session at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati. Dodgers management is hoping the session clears the last hurdle in Sasaki’s recovery from a right middle-finger blister that has sidelined him since the end of August.
A return to the active roster appears imminent, though the Dodgers haven’t decided whether he’ll resume his rotation spot or shift to the bullpen for the final weeks of the regular season.
Either way, Sasaki is expected to work exclusively out of the bullpen once the playoffs begin.
Sasaki could give manager Dave Roberts’ pitching staff a boost as the Dodgers gear up for October.
Before landing on the injured list, Sasaki posted a 4.60 ERA and 1.33 WHIP with 117 strikeouts over 119.1 innings across 23 starts. He was pulled from his Aug. 26 outing against the Atlanta Braves once the blister appeared. With a fastball averaging 97.8 mph and a plus splitter, Sasaki carries real swing-and-miss upside.
Bullpen an option
Should the Dodgers use him in the bullpen down the stretch, his triple-digit fastball and put-away splitter could bolster L.A.’s late-inning group immediately. Returning him to the rotation alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell would instead add starter depth and help manage workloads over the final two weeks of the regular season.
Keeping Sasaki’s finger healthy is a priority for the Dodgers front office, and avoiding another setback matters as the 24-year-old works his way back. Despite his inconsistent season, Sasaki has shown great stuff and figures to be a key piece of L.A.’s pitching staff as the postseason nears.
A clean live BP outing could lead to a short rehab assignment or a quicker activation before the Dodgers face the San Francisco Giants in their next series. Whether he lands in the rotation or the bullpen for the stretch run, the Dodgers will have another weapon at their disposal heading into October.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Shohei Ohtani, Carlos Correa and more: How star injuries could reshape the MLB playoffs

Carlos Correa is out. Max Fried is back. Shohei Ohtani is somewhere in-between. And questions linger ov
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- As October approaches, injuries and recoveries are poised to reshape the MLB postseason picture, with nearly every contender juggling critical absences and fragile returns.
- Houston shuts down Carlos Correa after an ankle setback, the Yankees finally get Max Fried and Aaron Judge back, while Shohei Ohtani looms as the Dodgers’ biggest question.
Carlos Correa is out. Max Fried is back. Shohei Ohtani is somewhere in-between. And questions linger over the postseason availability of several other MLB difference-makers as October approaches.
Here is a look at the injury status and hopeful returns of impact players on playoff qualifiers and contenders:
American League East
Tampa Bay Rays: Acquired from Baltimore at the trade deadline, swingman Tyler Wells posted a 1.50 earned-run-average before right forearm tightness sidelined him. He is back solely pitching from the bullpen, and could be a key piece for the Rays in their surprising surge to the division title.
Hopeful return: Slick-fielding shortstop Taylor Walls is recovering from a right hip flexor strain and signs point to him returning by October.
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
New York Yankees: The return of staff ace Fried is huge for a team that has clinched a wild-card berth and remains a long step behind the Rays for a division title and first-round bye. The left-hander out of Studio City Harvard-Westlake High gave up one run while walking none over seven innings in his longest start in almost five months. Fried has had two arduous IL stints dealing with a bone bruise on his left elbow.
Hopeful returns: Giancarlo Stanton or Trent Grisham returning in October would give the Yankees lineup additional pop. Three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge has been back for a week since missing more than three months with a fractured rib.
Boston Red Sox: A right quadriceps strain has kept All-Star center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela sidelined for two weeks. However, Rafaela told NESN that he expects to be activated this weekend, a substantial addition to a team that likely will play the Yankees in wild-card series.
Hopeful return: A year ago, Garrett Crochet was 18-5 and led the AL with 205 1/3 innings pitched. This year, left shoulder inflammation and a lat strain have kept him sidelined since April. However, he has ramped up bullpen sessions and is targeting a postseason return as a reliever.
American League Central
Chicago White Sox: The most improved team in baseball is desperately trying to hold off the Guardians and win a division title after finishing last two years in a row. Chicago has enjoyed good health and added journeyman outfielder Tommy Pham from the Phillies on Aug. 31. Pham was activated from the IL on Wednesday and could provide valuable postseason experience to complement his young new teammates — he has hit .315 in 37 career playoff games.
Hopeful return: Drew Thorpe was reinstated from the 60-day IL on Wednesday and is an intriguing option. The right-hander from Cal Poly SLO was a key piece in the 2024 trade that sent Dylan Cease to the Padres but has spent nearly two full seasons on the shelf. Now healthy, his inclusion on the playoff roster would be a gamble that his elite stuff can mask his inexperience.
Cleveland Guardians: Jo Adell didn’t come off the IL, but the addition of the former confounding Angels prospect in an August salary dump has bolstered the Guardians’ outfield — long a problem area. Adell has driven in 28 runs in 38 games with Cleveland and joins glittering rookie Chase DeLauter and steady veteran Steven Kwan in a productive outfield.
Hopeful return: Reliever Shawn Armstrong, who signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract last offseason, has been sidelined since July 24 with a calf strain. Barring a setback in his final minor league rehab appearance, he could be activated in time for the playoffs.
American League West
Houston Astros: Correa, whose second act with Houston has been a flop because of injuries, was working on an accelerated comeback from May ankle surgery. A few days ago team officials expressed optimism, but Tuesday they decided to shelve their shortstop when the ankle became inflamed after a workout. Houston is clinging to a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West.
Hopeful return: Nothing of note.
Texas Rangers: Still in contention despite spending much of the season under .500, the Rangers welcomed back pitcher Nathan Eovaldi and third baseman Josh Jung from the injured list over the weekend. A calf strain had kept Jung sidelined since July 21 and Eovaldi had been out since Aug. 7 with elbow inflammation. Eovaldi, who has started in all but 20 of his 339 MLB appearances, will pitch out of the bullpen.
Hopeful return: Nothing of note
National League East
Atlanta Braves: Reynaldo López inflated hopes of a late-career surge when he posted a 1.99 ERA over 25 starts in his first season with Atlanta. But injuries — including right shoulder inflammation this season — have severely limited his contribution. López was placed on the IL again Tuesday.
Hopeful return: Bryce Elder had an arthroscopic procedure to clean up bone fragments in his right knee on Sept. 8. The hope is that the right-handed starter can recover quickly enough to be counted upon in the postseason.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.
Philadelphia Phillies: Although an MRI found no structural damage to the throwing shoulder of stalwart starter Jesús Luzardo, the left-hander remains a question for the playoffs. He was placed on the 15-day IL retroactive to Sept. 12, and it is doubtful he could pitch again in the regular season. Luzardo has a 2.87 ERA across 29 starts this season.
Hopeful return: Tanner Banks, a major contributor to the Philadelphia bullpen in 2025, was reinstated from the 60-day IL over the weekend. Although he wasn’t effective earlier this season, Banks is welcomed back because Phillies relievers have been poor against left-handed hitters.
National League Central
Milwaukee Brewers: Huntington Beach Marina High product Jake Bauers has suffered from shin splints almost all season, and the pain has kept him from playing the outfield lately. He can play first base, but that takes slugger Andrew Vaughn out of the lineup. Bauers, with 26 home runs and 83 RBIs, has been a key bat for Milwaukee. He has been particularly tough against the Dodgers, batting .348 with a .483 on-base percentage.
Hopeful return: Brandon Woodruff, one of the best starters in baseball when healthy, is rehabbing from shoulder inflammation that sidelined him in July. The Brewers are nearly guaranteed a first-round bye, giving Woodruff an extra week to build stamina.
Chicago Cubs: Shortstop and team leader Dansby Swanson will be welcomed back after missing a month with a left oblique injury. He is expected to rejoin the Cubs during their weekend series against the Cincinnati Reds.
Hopeful return: Left-handed starter Justin Steele is progressing through bullpen sessions and is almost ready to take the mound after missing the entire season with a left elbow flexor strain. Steele, whose record was 16-5 in 2023, likely would pitch from the bullpen in the postseason.
National League West
Dodgers: The loss of center fielder Andy Pages is significant. He can bat near the top or bottom of the order, displays power and speed, and had improved his patience at the plate enough to earn a career-high 45 walks in 128 games.
Hopeful return: Getting Ohtani healthy enough to produce at the plate is a priority, and his absence from the mound shouldn’t be felt if Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow pitch to their capabilities. Meanwhile, Edwin Diaz might not even make the playoff roster.
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
San Diego Padres: While recovering from Tommy John surgery, starter Joe Musgrove made it a goal to be ready for the postseason. Recovery difficulties between starts have made his status doubtful, however. Nick Pivetta, on the other hand, has pitched well in two starts since coming off the IL and appears ready.
Hopeful return: Ramón Laurenano, a 2025 trade deadline acquisition with a potent bat, last played May 30 because of hip inflammation. However, he told reporters that the chances of him playing in the postseason are “less than 5%.”
Arizona Diamondbacks: Zac Gallen was activated from the 60-day IL and Michael Soroka from the 15-day IL, giving the D-Backs two starters in their push to win a wild-card berth. Gallen, a proven starter who has been horrendous in 2026, has been out since the All-Star break with elbow inflammation. Soroka was out only two weeks with the same ailment.
Hopeful return: Third baseman Nolan Arenado suffered an injury to his left thumb Tuesday, the same injury he sustained in late August. It’s doubtful the injury would sideline the 14-year veteran with games this week being so important, yet the Diamondbacks have to hope the injury doesn’t impact his productivity.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to win their series against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
The Dodgers took Monday's series opener, 4-1, behind seven shutout innings from Tarik Skubal. Then, they won Tuesday's game, 4-0, behind seven shutout innings from Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
On Wednesday, LA has another superstar pitcher on the mound in left-hander Blake Snell.
“When you’re writing in the lineup and you see those guys, and one trying to up the other guy, and then now you got Snell going [Wednesday] — you feel good about preventing runs,” manager Dave Roberts said.
“A team like the Reds right now, where they’re scuffling a little bit, it’s daunting when you see a starter like those guys that we’re running out there.”
Dodgers vs Reds Pitching Matchup on Wednesday
Snell is looking to continue his run of dominance since returning from midseason elbow surgery.
The left-hander has gone 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA across six starts, striking out 46 while allowing zero home runs over 34.2 innings of work.
Snell, who pitched 5.2 innings in his most recent start, is still looking to go deeper into games moving forward. He hasn't pitched more than six innings in any of his six starts.
“I mean the goal, at worst is definitely six for me,” Snell said. “I also know that I can go seven, eight, nine. I know I’m able to do it. So for me not to, I just have to get more efficient early in the game. I feel like once I get past the first couple innings, I start cruising and start figuring it out."
Opposite Snell will be left-hander Andrew Abbott, who's 6-11 with a 4.78 ERA and 120 strikeouts over 154.1 innings this season.
He's allowed seven earned runs in two of his last three starts, and has a 7.71 ERA since the start of August.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Tommy Edman, CF
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, DH
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, LF
Josue De Paula, Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound.

First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday, Sept. 16 is 3:40 p.m. PT/6:40 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers have glaring problems as playoffs approach — but also the threefold remedy
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The Dodgers will be in every game they play in October, and that alone means they will enter the playoffs as the favorites to win the World Series. Not because of Shohei Ohtani. Not because of Freddie Freeman. And certainly not because of their bullpen. There were a number of alarming developments in the last week or so, but if any team is designed to survive them, it’s the Dodgers. Whatever their problems, they still have the best rotation in baseball. No player influences the outcome of a game
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers will be in every game they play in October, and that alone means they will enter the playoffs as the favorites to win the World Series.
Not because of Shohei Ohtani. Not because of Freddie Freeman. And certainly not because of their bullpen.
There were a number of alarming developments in the last week or so, but if any team is designed to survive them, it’s the Dodgers.
Whatever their problems, they still have the best rotation in baseball.
No player influences the outcome of a game as much as a starting pitcher, and the Dodgers are the only team that will be able to roll out one Cy Young Award-caliber arm after another after another.
The Dodgers were negligent with Ohtani, and the verdict on their management of Freeman is pending, but they at least set up their pitchers the right way.
The rotation is more than a collection of big names. In Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell, the Dodgers have three starters who are peaking in time to deliver the kinds of performances that will be required for them to win their third consecutive World Series.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven shutout innings on Tuesday in a 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds, marking his third consecutive seven-inning start.
“I feel really good and I don’t have any physical problems,” Yamamoto told reporters in Japanese. “I want to treat practice each and every day with importance and go into October in the best condition.”
Yamamoto isn’t alone.
The day before Yamamoto’s start, Tarik Skubal pitched seven scoreless innings of his own in a 4-1 victory over the Reds. In his previous start, which was also against the Reds but at Dodger Stadium, Skubal pitched 7 ⅓ innings.
“Just getting in a rhythm,” Skubal said.
Blake Snell, who is scheduled to take his turn in the rotation on Wednesday, was 4-0 with a 1.04 earned-run average in the six games he started since returning from an elbow cleanup that cost him three months.
The one source of concern in the rotation is Tyler Glasnow, who, like Snell, was slow-played in his return from an injury. Sidelined for 3 ½ months because of back problems, Glasnow showed promise in his first couple of starts after he came back. But in his last two starts, he gave up a combined eight runs, 11 hits and seven walks in 10 innings. But as the team’s No. 4 starter, he is unlikely to start more than one game in any postseason series.
Even before Ohtani was placed on the injured list because of right arm and left knee injuries, the starting pitching was likely going to have to carry the Dodgers – much as it did last year.
Recent developments have shifted even more of the burden to the starting pitchers.
Edwin Diaz, their $69-million closer, was blow-torched for five runs in ⅔ of an inning in the most recent game of his minor-league rehabilitation assignment. At this point, he’s a longshot to make the postseason roster.
Diaz’s failure to rediscover his All-Star form will have major ramifications on the bullpen, which lost ninth-inning candidate Edgardo Henriquez to a lower-back problem for the remainder of the regular season. Henriquez’s status for the playoffs remains a mystery.
Manager Dave Roberts’ current ninth-inning choice, Tanner Scott, is in a minor slump, as he has given up runs in five of his last 12 apperances.
While the Dodgers will have to find a closer – Roki Sasaki? – their ability to create favorable matchups in the innings before the ninth is also under question. The simplest way to address those uncertainties will be for the starters to pitch deeper into games. Last year, Yamamoto pitched a complete game in the National League Championship Series and another in his next start in the World Series. Snell had an eight-inning start in the NLCS.
The greater problem could be the already-inconsistent offense, which could go into the playoffs with physically-compromised versions of Ohtani and Freeman.
Freeman missed three of five games before starting at first base on Tuesday. Freeman collected three hits in the game, but he’s 37 years old and the Dodgers can’t be certain how his right knee will hold up.
As for Ohtani, Roberts reported on Tuesday that he resumed baseball activities. Roberts said he expected Ohtani to return before the end of the regular season, but hedged his prediction.
“Whether it happens or not,” Roberts said, “is to be determined.”
If the Dodgers don’t know if Ohtani will be able to even step into the batter’s box next week, how could they possibly count on him to be a consistent source of offense?
They can’t.
In other words, the margin for error could be miniscule for the Dodgers. Their starting pitchers might have to be close to perfect. The challenge will be formidable. But considering who will be pitching for them, it will be very much in the realm of possibility.

And it doesn’t get much easier with Blake Snell taking the mound, as the Dodgers are one win away from sweeping the Reds in a fourth straight series dating back to last year—counting both the regular season and playoffs. Considering Sunday’s loss to the Marlins in which Emmet Sheehan pitched quite well, Dodger starters have held oppon
item.content:encoded:
The colloquially called “Great American Small Park” has looked awfully big for the Cincinnati Reds hitters facing the best pitching that the Dodgers have to offer. And it doesn’t get much easier with Blake Snell taking the mound, as the Dodgers are one win away from sweeping the Reds in a fourth straight series dating back to last year—counting both the regular season and playoffs.
Considering Sunday’s loss to the Marlins in which Emmet Sheehan pitched quite well, Dodger starters have held opponents scoreless through 20 innings, 14 of which have come against starters Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. On top of being dominant, Skubal and Yamamoto share the fact that they deviated somewhat from their regular approach in their last outing against the Reds, but in opposite directions—Skubal leaning more heavily on the fastball, while Yamamoto threw it even less than he normally does.
A critical distinction must be made between these two previous starters and Snell. Unlike the pair, Snell will be facing the Reds for the first time this season since he was not on the schedule in the three-game series at Dodger Stadium last week. And speaking of a track record against the Reds, Snell will have fond memories of his last time pitching at this stadium. Back in 2024, still with the Giants, Snell delivered one of the greatest outings of his career when he shut out the Reds in a 3-0 win—the two-time Cy Young winner punched out 11 in what, to this day, remains the only complete game and the only shutout of Snell’s illustrious career.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yoshinobu Yamamoto Shows Dodgers Exactly Why He Should Start Game 1

A day after the Dodgers clinched their postseason berth and secured a shot at completing their three-peat, Yamamoto took the mound to help the team in their postseason seeding race with a road game against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday, September 16th. Yamamoto went seven scoreless innings, allowing one hit and two walks while getting ei
item.content:encoded:
When he needed it most, starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto reminded everyone in the Los Angeles Dodgers clubhouse why he is the man for Game 1 of any playoff series.
A day after the Dodgers clinched their postseason berth and secured a shot at completing their three-peat, Yamamoto took the mound to help the team in their postseason seeding race with a road game against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday, September 16th.
Yamamoto went seven scoreless innings, allowing one hit and two walks while getting eight punchouts, and looked like he had much more in the tank.
Manager Dave Roberts could have easily kept Yamamoto in for at least another inning; the Japanese pitcher had only 91 pitches down, given his propensity to pitch a high volume.
He allowed only two hard hits, highlighting his dominance, and both walks came on his first two batters.
Yamamoto retired 21 of the final 22 batters he faced, threw 16 whiffs, and used a wide variety of pitches, with none exceeding 25% usage.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto had another great outing, his best one in a while:
7 IP
1 H
2 BB
7 Ks
He looked great and could have gone another inning on just 91 pitches.
Quick and efficient from the Dodgers' ace. pic.twitter.com/pro7lpwsiK
The outing was a nice change of pace for Yamamoto, who has been prone to the long ball and giving up hard contact.
Instead, he did a good job of keeping the Reds hitters off-balance, and it looked like what Dodger fans have come to expect from Yamamoto: efficiency, elite pitch mix, and weak contact.
Why Dave Roberts Trusts Yamamoto
More than anything, his ability to move on from mistakes, like his lack of command that led to two walks right off the bat, is really the special sauce for Yamamoto.
Roberts, after the game, spoke to this resilience and how it translates perfectly to October and high-leverage moments, when everyone gets tested in some shape or fashion.
"I think the thing that I've learned about Yoshinobu is he's able to reset on the fly," the skipper said.
"He's able to bear down and make pitches when he needs to, to get a double play, a strikeout, a pop-up.
"Those are separators. When you're not totally locked in or in sync, you can still take a deep breath, reset, and navigate an inning and keep going. And so that's something that I've really learned from him."
Why Yamamoto Needed This Outing Now
Given his 2025 postseason exploits, it is hard to argue that Yamamoto has much to prove in the playoffs, and he needs to make his case to pitch the first game in the postseason.
Pitching in Game 1, when the team is fully healthy, is the ultimate nod of respect for an ace, and earning that honor as a member of his special rotation makes it all the more noteworthy.
Yamamoto, given his track record, has seemingly been in pole position all season, but Blake Snell's form and Tarik Skubal's arrival have sparked a healthy debate about who takes the ball first.
Since returning from the IL after elbow surgery on August 11th, Snell has a 1.04 ERA through 34.2 innings. He has 46 strikeouts and 14 walks in that span.
Yamamoto has a 1.98 ERA in 68.1 innings since the All-Star break. His ratio is 72 strikeouts to 16 walks.
By comparison, Skubal has a 2.52 ERA in 50 innings with the Dodgers since joining from the trade deadline on August 3rd. He also has a 57 strikeouts-to-11 walks ratio.
Recently, Skubal had his own seven-inning scoreless outing, and he looked very settled in, while Snell has not put a foot wrong.
However, Yamamoto's latest outing showed the front office that he can deliver a vintage Yamamoto outing, which, come postseason time, is invaluable.
It means he can provide a long outing, sometimes a complete game, along with minimal runs allowed, and leave the hitters in a tizzy.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Blake Snell, Dodgers look to clinch NL West title against Reds
item.dc:creator: FLM

item.content:encoded:
With a chance to clinch their 13th division title in 14 straight playoff seasons, the Los Angeles Dodgers will start a pitcher who threw a no-hitter in his most recent start on the mound he will be on Wednesday night in Cincinnati.
Left-hander Blake Snell (4-1, 1.91 ERA) will return to Great American Ball Park, where he no-hit the Cincinnati Reds on Aug. 2, 2024, as a member of the San Francisco Giants. Now with the Dodgers, the veteran southpaw will look to create that magic again as Los Angeles positions itself for a deep postseason run.
That night in 2024, Snell struck out 11 and walked three in San Francisco's 3-0 win, which concluded when Elly De La Cruz flied out to right-center. Snell will face Cincinnati for the first time since he started Game 1 of the National League wild-card series last season, holding Cincinnati to two runs and four hits over seven innings of a 10-5 win for host Los Angeles. Snell struck out nine and walked one.
The two-time Cy Young Award winner has completed at least five innings and hasn't allowed more than one earned run in each of his six starts since his return from May arthroscopic surgery, which removed loose bodies in his left elbow. He has allowed a total of just four runs and has 46 strikeouts across 34 2/3 innings and has a 4-0 record and 1.04 ERA since then.
The 33-year-old veteran struck out eight, walked two and allowed four hits and one run over 5 2/3 innings in his most recent start, a 6-2 victory last Friday against the Miami Marlins.
"I think I can be way better," Snell said. "I think it's going good because just pitching in this league so much, I understand hitters, and I'm starting to adjust quicker, which I'm getting excited about. I go out there with a plan and being able to adjust and get quick outs off of that, or get ahead to get strikeouts. It's starting to get quicker, which I'm extremely happy about."
The Dodgers (92-59) have won all five meetings with the Reds this season and are trying to catch the Milwaukee Brewers (94-57) for the best overall record in the major leagues this season.
Also, a Dodgers win or a San Diego Padres loss on Wednesday would clinch the fifth straight NL West title for the Dodgers, who have champagne waiting for them outside the visitors' clubhouse in Cincinnati.
The mood is much different for the Reds (70-81), who lost 4-0 to the Dodgers on Tuesday following a 4-1 loss in the opener of a four-game series on Monday. Tuesday's shutout was the Reds' 17th of the season. Cincinnati has dropped seven of its past eight games to fall to a season-low 11 games below .500.
The Reds on Wednesday will send a left-hander of their own to the mound in Andrew Abbott (6-11, 4.78 ERA), making his career-high 31st start of the season. It has been a volatile campaign for the 27-year-old Abbott, who has given up 24 home runs and has only 11 quality starts.
Abbott is coming off a nightmarish outing against the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday. He was tagged for eight runs (seven earned) on nine hits in just two innings during a 20-0 blowout loss.
"The only good thing I did was throw strikes, but I was in the zone too much," Abbott said. "I let the team down by getting yanked in the second after such a bad start. That didn't feel good."
De La Cruz had two of Cincinnati's three hits on Tuesday and has an MLB-leading 22-game on-base streak.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers’ winning ways in September were briefly interrupted for two games against the Miami Marlins, but they have picked back up against the Cincinnati Reds, taking the first two games of a four-game set.
After Tarik Skubal shut down Cincinnati over seven innings on Monday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued the trend of marvelous results from the rotation with a seven-inning scoreless gem on Tuesday, working through a pair of lead-off walks while allowing just one hit while striking out seven. Yamamoto has amazed in his two most recent starts— both against the Reds— allowing just one run over 14 innings while racking up 17 strikeouts compared to just three walks.
Yamamoto held the Reds to just a 1-21 clip after walking his first two hitters of the game on Tuesday, and the right-hander managed to take a page out of Skubal’s playbook for his dominating efforts, notes Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
Yamamoto was able to learn from how the Reds approached Skubal the night before, and Snell was no doubt gathering similar information on Tuesday.
“That kind of encouraged me to be aggressive and attack the hitters,” Yamamoto said through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda.
The pitching has managed to hold their end of the bargain against Cincinnati this week, and Blake Snell looks to keep that trajectory in motion. On the offensive side of the ball, Teoscar Hernández has fortified the offense at Great American Ball Park, as the right-hander has crushed a pair of two-run home runs that put both games out of reach.
Hernández has once again found his stride that fans saw during spring training this year, and the Dodger outfielder’s recent success is the brainchild of hitting coach Aaron Bates, allowing Hernández to have a “twister tap” in his stride to the ball, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
Update on Shohei Ohtani
It’s an unusual feeling watching the Dodgers without Shohei Ohtani in the everyday lineup. So far, rookie Josue De Paula has filled in at DH to a small degree of success in limited time (.143/.368/.429, 19 PA) while the reigning two-time NL MVP recovers from multiple nagging issues.
Jack Harris of the California Post notes that Ohtani was able to take batting practice on Monday, and the team is optimistic that he can potentially return from the injured list before the end of the regular season.
“Today was positive,” Roberts said, “and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”

item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one hit through seven innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-0 on Tuesday night to edge closer to an NL West division title.
The Dodgers reduced the magic number to clinch their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons to two. Los Angeles wrapped up a playoff spot on Monday and still is vying for the top seed in the NL.
Cincinnati is assured of a non-winning season after its 81st loss.
Yamamoto (14-8) made his team-high 27th start and allowed only a third-inning double to Elly De La Cruz, after which he retired 10 straight. He walked two and struck out seven. It was the second straight game a Dodgers starter went seven scoreless after Tarik Skubal on Monday.
Dodgers pitching recorded its 12th shutout of the season. The Reds were blanked for the 17th time.
Freddie Freeman returned to the Dodgers lineup after missing three of the past five games with right knee soreness and had three singles in five at-bats. Freeman was 3 for 30 coming into Tuesday.
Josue De Paula batted leadoff for the first time in just his fifth career game for the Dodgers and went 0 for 5 with a strikeout. He's 2 for 14 since his callup.
Teoscar Hernandez's 15th homer of the season off right-hander Rhett Lowder followed a walk to Kyle Tucker and made the score 3-0 in the third. Lowder (6-11) allowed three earned runs on five hits in five innings.
Alex Freeland made the score 4-0 in the seventh with a solo homer off Pierce Johnson.
De La Cruz extended his on-base streak to 22 games dating to Aug. 22, going 2 for 3 with a double, walk, and stolen base.
Cincinnati had runners on first and third in the ninth against Tanner Scott who struck out the next three batters to seal the Dodgers' ninth straight win over the Reds.
Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.91) will oppose Reds LHP Andrew Abbott (6-11, 4.84) on Wednesday.

item.content:encoded:
Teoscar Hernández volvió a demostrar que atraviesa un momento ofensivo importante y encabezó la ofensiva de los Dodgers en la victoria 4-0 sobre los Reds este martes en el Great American Ball Park.
El dominicano conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras en la tercera entrada, su segundo vuelacercas en igual cantidad de partidos, para ampliar una ventaja que Los Ángeles ya no perdería.
Hernández terminó de 3-1 y produjo dos carreras, mientras los Dodgers se acercaron a solo dos victorias de asegurar el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
El jonrón tuvo además un significado particular para Hernández, quien había tenido dificultades frente a los lanzadores derechos durante buena parte de la temporada. Hasta finales de agosto, registraba apenas .668 de OPS contra derechos, situación que incluso llevó al manager Dave Roberts a considerar un posible pelotón en el jardín izquierdo con jugadores recién ascendidos.
Después de conectar un jonrón ante el zurdo Framber Valdez en Detroit, Hernández trabajó con los coaches de bateo antes de la serie contra los Cardinals, y desde entonces su producción ha comenzado a cambiar.
Yamamoto intransitable
La actuación del dominicano sirvió como complemento perfecto para otra extraordinaria presentación de Yoshinobu Yamamoto. El japonés tuvo un comienzo poco habitual, al fallar ocho de sus primeros nueve lanzamientos y conceder boletos consecutivos a los dos primeros bateadores de Cincinnati. Fue apenas la cuarta ocasión esta temporada en que otorgó múltiples boletos en una entrada y la primera vez en su carrera de Grandes Ligas que abrió una salida con dos bases por bolas consecutivas.
Pero aquel descontrol inicial quedó rápidamente en el pasado. Después de poner a dos corredores en las bases en el primer episodio, Yamamoto solo permitió que otro bateador de Cincinnati llegara a salvo durante el resto de su actuación. Retiró a 21 de los últimos 22 bateadores que enfrentó y completó siete entradas en blanco, con apenas un hit permitido, un doble de Elly De La Cruz en el tercer inning, además de siete ponches.
La ofensiva angelina había tomado ventaja desde el segundo episodio, cuando Hunter Feduccia produjo una carrera con un sencillo. En el tercero llegó el batazo de Hernández para colocar el marcador 3-0 y, posteriormente, Alex Freeland agregó otro cuadrangular solitario para completar las cuatro carreras de Los Ángeles. El ataque de los Dodgers no fue especialmente abundante, pero produjo lo suficiente para respaldar a Yamamoto y convertir su actuación en una nueva joya monticular.
Para Yamamoto, fue además su tercera apertura consecutiva completando siete entradas y la quinta salida seguida en la que alcanzó al menos el séptimo episodio. Desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas, el derecho japonés ha mantenido un ritmo dominante, con efectividad de 1.98 en 68? entradas, 72 ponches y solo 16 boletos en 10 aperturas, una producción que lo coloca como una de las principales piezas de la rotación de Los Ángeles de cara a octubre.
La victoria dejó a los Dodgers con el número mágico en dos para conquistar su decimotercer título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas.
- Después de haber asegurado ya su boleto a la postemporada, Los Ángeles continúa ahora en busca de la corona divisional y de una posición privilegiada para octubre.
Blake Snell será el encargado de subir al montículo en el próximo encuentro de la serie, mientras los Dodgers siguen construyendo una rotación que, con Yamamoto al frente, vuelve a tomar protagonismo en su búsqueda de un tercer campeonato consecutivo.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers’ bullpen combine on 3-hit shutout to beat Reds
